**Tafsir of Surah Maryam [peace be upon her]** [[Addition from manuscripts T, F, and A.]]

It is a Meccan surah.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq related in *al-Sirah* (the Life of the Prophet), on the authority of Umm Salamah, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal related on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud, in the account of the migration to the land of Abyssinia from Makkah, that Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, recited the opening of this surah to the Negus (al-Najashi) and his companions. [[Ahmad narrated it from the hadith of Umm Salamah (5/290) and from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud (1/461).]]

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

* *

As for the discussion of the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah), it has already been covered at the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah.

* *

His saying: ﴿This is a mention of the mercy of your Lord﴾, meaning: this is a mention of Allah's mercy toward His servant Zakariyya.

Yahya ibn Ya'mar recited it as: "Dhakkara rahmata Rabbika 'abdahu Zakariyya" (He recounted the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zakariyya).

﴿Zakariyya﴾: the word may be read with a long vowel (yumaddu) or a short vowel (yuqsaru); both are well-known readings. He was a great prophet among the prophets of the Children of Israel. In Sahih al-Bukhari it is related that he was a carpenter (najjar), meaning that he would eat from the work of his hands in carpentry.

* *

His saying: ﴿when he called to his Lord with a secret call﴾. Some of the exegetes said: he only made his supplication in secret so that he would not be regarded as foolish in seeking a child because of his old age. This is related by al-Mawardi.

Others said: he made it secret because it is more beloved to Allah. As Qatadah said regarding this verse, ﴿when he called to his Lord with a secret call﴾: Allah knows the pure heart and hears the hidden voice.

Some of the early scholars (al-salaf) said: he, peace be upon him, rose during the night while his companions were asleep, and he began calling upon his Lord in a whisper, saying: "O Lord, O Lord, O Lord." Then Allah said: "Here I am, here I am, here I am."

﴿He said: "My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened within me"﴾, meaning: they have become weak and his strength has failed; ﴿and my head has glistened with grey hair﴾, meaning: the greyness has spread through the blackness, as Ibn Duraid said in his *Maqsurah*:

*When you see my head, its colour resembles*
*the dawn's streak beneath the skirts of the night...*

*The white has blazed through its blackness*
*like the blazing of fire in the embers of the ghada tree...* [[Ghada is a desert tree. See *Sharh Maqsurat Ibn Duraid* (p. 2), as cited in the margin of the Shu'ab edition.]]

The purpose of this is to report his weakness and old age, and its outward and inward signs.

* *

His saying: ﴿And I have never been unsuccessful in my supplication to You, my Lord﴾, meaning: I have known from You only the answering of supplication, and You have never turned me away in anything I have asked of You.

* *

His saying: ﴿And indeed I fear my successors after me﴾. Most readers recited the "ya'" of ﴿al-mawali﴾ with a fatha, as the object. It is related from al-Kisa'i that he pronounced the "ya'" with a sukun, as the poet said:

*As if their hands in the qa' Farq*
*were hands of maidens picking leaves...* [[The verse is in *Lisan al-Arab* under *qarq*, without attribution.]]

Another said:

*A youth who, if he were to vie with the sun, it would cast off its veil,*
*or with the traveling moon, it would cast off its necklaces...*

And from this is the saying of Abu Tammam Habib ibn Aws al-Ta'i:

*Poetry varied in him when I stayed awake for it,*
*until I thought its rhymes would fight one another...* [[The verse is in *Diwan Abi Tammam* (227), as cited in the margin of the Shu'ab edition.]]

Mujahid, Qatadah, and al-Suddi said: by "al-mawali" is meant the agnatic relatives (al-'asabah). Abu Salih said: it means the kalalah (collateral heirs).

It is related from the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, that he used to recite it: "wa inni khafat al-mawali min wara'i" with a shaddah on the "fa'", meaning: my agnatic relatives have diminished after me.

According to the first reading, the reason for his fear is that he feared they would manage the affairs of the people after him in a bad way. So he asked Allah for a child who would be a prophet after him, to govern them with his prophethood and with what is revealed to him. He was answered in this matter. It was not that he feared they would inherit his wealth, for the prophet is of far too great a station and too exalted a rank to be concerned for his wealth to such an extent that he would be averse to his agnatic relatives inheriting from him, and would ask for a son so that the son would take his inheritance to the exclusion of them. This is one opinion.

The second: it is not mentioned that he possessed wealth; rather he was a carpenter who ate from the earnings of his hands, and such a person does not accumulate wealth, especially the prophets, peace be upon them, for they were the most detached from this world.

The third: it has been established in the two Sahihs through more than one chain that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "We prophets are not inherited from; what we leave behind is charity." [[It comes from the hadith of Aisha, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Umar ibn al-Khattab, Talhah, Uthman ibn Affan, and al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam. The hadith of Aisha is narrated by al-Bukhari (6730) and Muslim (1758). The hadith of Abu Bakr is narrated by al-Bukhari (1/37) and Muslim (1759). The hadith of Umar, Uthman, Talhah, and al-Zubayr is narrated by al-Bukhari (3094, 6728, 7305) and Muslim (1757).]] In a narration in al-Tirmidhi with a sahih chain: "We, the company of prophets, are not inherited from." [[I did not find this wording in the printed *Sunan al-Tirmidhi*. See the discussion of Hafiz Ibn Hajar regarding this narration and the meanings it may bear in *Fath al-Bari* (12/8).]] Given this, the saying ﴿So grant me from Yourself an heir, who will inherit from me﴾ must be understood as the inheritance of prophethood. For this reason He said: ﴿and will inherit from the family of Ya'qub﴾, just as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Sulayman inherited from Dawud﴾ [An-Naml: 16], meaning in prophethood. For if it were inheritance of wealth, he would not have singled him out from among his brothers for it, and there would have been no great benefit in reporting it, since it is well known and established in all the laws and religions that a son inherits from his father. So were it not a special inheritance, it would not have been reported. All of this is confirmed and established by the sound hadith: "We, the company of prophets, are not inherited from; what we leave behind is charity."

Mujahid said regarding His saying: ﴿who will inherit from me and inherit from the family of Ya'qub﴾: his inheritance was knowledge, and Zakariyya was a descendant of Ya'qub.

Hushaym said: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid informed us, from Abu Salih regarding His saying: ﴿who will inherit from me and inherit from the family of Ya'qub﴾, he said: he may become a prophet, just as his forefathers were prophets.

Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan: he inherits his prophethood and his knowledge.

Al-Suddi said: he inherits my prophethood and the prophethood of the family of Ya'qub.

It is related from Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam: ﴿and inherit from the family of Ya'qub﴾, he said: their prophethood.

Jabir ibn Nuh and Yazid ibn Harun both said, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih regarding His saying: ﴿who will inherit from me and inherit from the family of Ya'qub﴾, he said: he inherits my wealth, and from the family of Ya'qub he inherits prophethood.

This is the preference of Ibn Jarir in his *Tafsir*.

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, said: "May Allah have mercy upon Zakariyya; what was his concern with the heirs of his wealth?" and "May Allah have mercy upon Lut; he would indeed take refuge in a strong pillar." [[*Tafsir* of Abd al-Razzaq (2/5). Its second part has been connected: "May Allah have mercy upon Lut; he would indeed take refuge in a strong pillar." Imam Ahmad in his *Musnad* (2/350) through the route of al-Zuhri, from Sa'id and Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, from Mubarak (that is, Ibn Fudalah), from al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, said: "May Allah have mercy upon my brother Zakariyya; what was his concern with the heirs of his wealth when he said: ﴿So grant me from Yourself an heir, who will inherit from me and inherit from the family of Ya'qub﴾." [[*Tafsir al-Tabari* (16/37).]] These are mursal reports which do not contradict the sound (sahih) reports, and Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿and make him, my Lord, pleasing﴾, meaning: one who is pleasing to You and to Your creation, whom You love and whom You make beloved to Your creation, in his religion and his character.

This is the preference of Ibn Jarir in his *Tafsir*.

[[*Tafsir al-Tabari* (16/37).]] These are mursal reports which do not contradict the sound (sahih) reports, and Allah knows best.

His saying: ﴿and make him, my Lord, pleasing﴾, meaning: one who is pleasing to You and to Your creation, whom You love and whom You make beloved to Your creation, in his religion and his character.

This statement implies an omitted part, namely that he was granted what he asked for in his supplication, and it was said to him: ﴿O Zakariyya, indeed We give you good tidings of a boy whose name is Yahya﴾, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿There Zakariyya called upon his Lord, saying, "My Lord, grant me from Yourself good offspring. Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication." So the angels called to him while he stood praying in the sanctuary, "Indeed, Allah gives you good tidings of Yahya, confirming a word from Allah, and a noble leader, and chaste, and a prophet from among the righteous."﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 38, 39]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿We have not made for him before a namesake﴾, Qatadah, Ibn Juraij and Ibn Zayd said: meaning no one before him was named with this name. Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, chose this interpretation.

Mujahid said: ﴿We have not made for him before a namesake﴾ means: a like or an equal. He took this from the meaning of His saying: ﴿So worship Him and be steadfast in His worship. Do you know of any equal to Him?﴾ [Maryam: 65], meaning: an equal.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: meaning, the barren women had not borne anyone before him like him.

This is evidence that Zakariyya (peace be upon him) could not have children, and likewise his wife was barren from the beginning of her life. This differs from Ibrahim and Sarah (peace be upon them), for they were only amazed at the good tidings of Ishaq because of their old age, not because of barrenness. Therefore He said: ﴿Do you give me good tidings although old age has touched me? Then by what will you give good tidings?﴾ [al-Hijr: 54], even though Isma'il had been born to him thirteen years earlier. And his wife said: ﴿Woe to me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman and this, my husband, is an old man? Indeed, this is an amazing thing!﴾ They said: ﴿Do you wonder at the decree of Allah? The mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, O people of the house. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Glorious.﴾ [Hud: 72, 73].

This is an expression of wonder from Zakariyya (peace be upon him), when his request was granted and he was given the good news of a child. He rejoiced greatly, and he asked about the manner in which a child would be born to him and the way it would come to him, given that his wife had been barren and had not borne a child from the beginning of her life, and she was now advanced in age. He himself had grown old and become feeble, meaning that his bones had weakened and dried up, and no vitality or capacity for intercourse remained in him.

The Arabs say of a branch when it dries out: "'ataa ya'tu 'itiyyan wa 'utuwwan" (عتا يعتو عتيا وعتوا), and "'asaa ya'su 'usuwwan wa 'isiyyan" (وعسا يعسو عسوا وعسيا).

Mujahid said: ﴿feebleness﴾ (عتيا) means the wasting away of the bones.

Ibn Abbas and others said: ﴿feebleness﴾ (عتيا) means old age.

The apparent meaning is that it is more specific than old age.

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub told us, Hushaym told us, Husayn informed us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "I have known the whole Sunnah, except that I do not know whether the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited in the Dhuhr and 'Asr prayers or not, and I do not know how he recited this letter: ﴿and I have indeed reached extreme old age﴾ (عتيا), or 'asiyyan' (عسيا)."

Ahmad narrated it from Suraij ibn al-Nu'man, and Abu Dawud from Ziyad ibn Ayyub, both from Hushaym, with the same chain.

This also (implies) an omitted element. Its implied sense is: that he found this boy who had been given good news of, who is Yahya, peace be upon him, and that Allah taught him the Book, which is the Torah that they used to study among themselves, and by which the prophets who submitted to the Lord (*alladhina aslamu lilladhina hadu*) and the rabbis (*rabbaniyyun*) and the scholars (*ahbar*) judge. At that time he was still young, so He highlighted his mention and what He had bestowed upon him and upon his parents, saying: ﴿O Yahya, take the Book with strength﴾, that is, learn the Book ﴿with strength﴾, that is, with earnestness, eagerness and diligence. ﴿And We gave him judgment while still a boy﴾, that is, understanding, knowledge, earnestness, resolve, turning toward good, devoting oneself to it, and striving in it while he was still young in age.

[Editorial note: in A, the word is "yadmunu" (يضمن); in T it is "yadmun."]

Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: Ma'mar said: The children said to Yahya ibn Zakariyya, "Come, let us play." He said, "I was not created for play." He said: Therefore Allah revealed: ﴿And We gave him judgment while still a boy﴾.

[Editorial note: in F and A, it reads "khuliqna" (we were created).]

As for His saying: ﴿And tenderness from Us﴾, Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And tenderness from Us﴾ means mercy from Us. Ikrimah, Qatadah and al-Dahhak said the same, and al-Dahhak added: none can grant it but Us. Qatadah added: Zakariyya was shown mercy through him.

Mujahid said: ﴿And tenderness from Us﴾, and compassion from his Lord toward him.

Ikrimah said: ﴿And tenderness from Us﴾ [he said: affection for him]. Ibn Zayd said: As for *hanan*, it is affection. Ata ibn Abi Rabah said: ﴿And tenderness from Us﴾, he said: magnification from Us.

[Editorial note: in A, it reads "al-dunya" (the world).]

Ibn Jurayj said: Amr ibn Dinar informed me that he heard Ikrimah narrate from Ibn Abbas that he said: "No, by Allah, I do not know what *hanan* means."

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about His saying: ﴿And tenderness from Us﴾, and he said: I asked Ibn Abbas about it, but he did not say anything about it.

The apparent meaning of the context is that ﴿and tenderness from Us﴾ is conjoined to His saying ﴿We gave him judgment while still a boy﴾, meaning: We gave him judgment and tenderness, ﴿and purity﴾, meaning: We made him one possessing tenderness and purity. *Hanan* is affection with compassion and inclination, as the Arabs say: "the she-camel yearned (*hannat*) over her offspring," and "the woman yearned over her husband." From this comes the name "Hanna" for a woman, from *hinna* (henna). A man yearns (*hanna*) for his homeland. From it also comes tenderness and mercy, as the poet said:

*Tahannan 'alayya hadaka al-malik... fa-inna li-kulli maqamin maqalan*
(May the King show tenderness toward me, for every situation has its own speech.)

[Editorial note: in F it reads "ta'attuf" (tenderness).]

In the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A man will remain in the Fire calling for a thousand years: O Hannan, O Mannan."

[Source note: Musnad (3/230).]

Some have made the repetition *hananan*, or some take what occurs of this to be a language of its own, as Tarafa said:

*Ana Mundhir, afnayta fa-istabqi ba'dana... hananayka ba'd al-shar ahwanu min ba'd*
(I am Mundhir; you have consumed, so spare some of us. Your *hananayk* (tenderness of yours): some evil is easier than other evil.)

[Source note: the verse is in his Diwan (p. 208); from the margin of the Shi'b edition.]

As for His saying: ﴿And purity﴾, it is conjoined to ﴿and tenderness﴾. *Zakah* is purity from defilement, sins and wrongdoings.

Qatadah said: *Zakah* is righteous deeds.

Al-Dahhak and Ibn Jurayj said: righteous deeds that are pure.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And purity﴾ [he said: blessing], ﴿and he was devout﴾, pure, so he did not commit a sin.

As for His saying: ﴿And dutiful to his parents, and he was not a tyrant, a disobedient one﴾: when Exalted is He mentioned his obedience to his Lord, and that He created him possessing mercy, purity and piety, He followed with the mention of his obedience to his parents, his kindness toward them, and his avoidance of disobeying them, in word and deed, in command and prohibition. For this reason He said: ﴿and he was not a tyrant, a disobedient one﴾. Then, after these beautiful attributes, He said as a reward for that: ﴿And peace be upon him the day he was born, the day he dies, and the day he is raised alive﴾, that is, security is his in these three states.

Sufyan ibn Uyayna said: Creatures are most desolate in three places: the day one is born, when he sees himself coming out of what he was in; the day he dies, when he sees people he had not seen; and the day he is raised, when he sees himself in a great gathering. He said: Allah honored Yahya ibn Zakariyya in these, singling him out with peace upon him: ﴿And peace be upon him the day he was born, the day he dies, and the day he is raised alive﴾.

Ibn Jarir narrated it from Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Marwazi, from Sadaqah ibn al-Fadl, from him.

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿tyrant, disobedient﴾: Ibn al-Musayyab used to mention, saying: The Prophet ﷺ said: "There is no one who meets Allah on the Day of Resurrection except one who has a sin, except Yahya ibn Zakariyya." Qatadah said: He did not sin, nor did he intend to be with a woman. (This is a *mursal* report.)

[Source note: Tafsir Abd al-Razzaq (2/7).]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: Ibn al-'As narrated to me that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Every child of Adam will come on the Day of Resurrection with a sin, except what belongs to Yahya ibn Zakariyya."

[Source note: narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (16/44) and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (2/373) through Muhammad ibn Ishaq. Al-Hakim said: "This is a sound hadith according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it." Al-Dhahabi agreed. Abu Hatim preferred that it stops at the companion level and said to his son: "They do not raise this hadith."] Ibn Ishaq here is a *mudallis* (one who conceals defects in transmission), and he has reported this hadith with *an'ana* (ambiguous wording), so Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Ali ibn Zayd informed us, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no one from the children of Adam except that he has erred, or intended a sin, except Yahya ibn Zakariyya. And it is not befitting for anyone to say: I am better than Yunus ibn Matta."

[Source note: al-Musnad (1/254).]

This is also weak, because Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an has many rejected reports, and Allah knows best.

Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah said, from Qatadah, that al-Hasan said: Yahya and Isa, peace be upon them both, met, and Isa said to him: "Ask forgiveness for me, for you are better than me." The other said: "You ask forgiveness for me, for you are better than me." Isa said to him: "You are better than me; I greeted myself with peace, and Allah has greeted you with peace." By Allah, their merit became known.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 19, verse 16–21:

When Allah the Exalted mentioned the story of Zakariyya (ʿalayhi as-salam), and that He brought forth from him, in his old age and his wife's barrenness, a pure, blessed, righteous son, He followed it with the mention of the story of Maryam in bringing forth her son ʿIsa, upon them both be peace, from her without a father. The two stories have a correspondence and a similarity (munasabah wa mushabahah). For this reason He mentioned them both in Surat Al ʿImran, here, and in Surat al-Anbiya', linking the two stories because of the closeness of their meaning, to show His servants His power and the greatness of His dominion, and that He is capable of whatever He wills. So He said: ﴿And mention in the Book Maryam﴾. She is Maryam bint ʿImran, of the lineage of Dawud (ʿalayhi as-salam), and she was from a pure, good household among the Children of Israel. Allah the Exalted has mentioned the story of her mother's giving birth to her in Surat Al ʿImran, and that her mother dedicated her as one freed (muharraran), meaning she would serve the Masjid of Bayt al-Maqdis, and they used to seek nearness to Allah through that: ﴿So her Lord accepted her with a good acceptance and caused her to grow in a good growth﴾ [Al ʿImran: 37]. She grew up among the Children of Israel in a great upbringing, and she was one of the worshipping, devout women, famous for great worship, devotion (tabattul) and diligence. She was under the guardianship of the husband of her sister—and it was said: her aunt—Zakariyya, the prophet of the Children of Israel at that time and their great one, to whom they would refer in their religion. Zakariyya saw from her such awesome marvels (karamat) that amazed him: ﴿Every time Zakariyya entered upon her in the prayer niche (mihrab), he found with her provision. He said, "O Maryam, from where is this for you?" She said, "It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account"﴾ [Al ʿImran: 37]. It is mentioned that he would find with her the fruit of winter in summer and the fruit of summer in winter, as was explained earlier in Surat Al ʿImran.

When Allah the Exalted—and to Him belong wisdom and conclusive proof—willed to bring forth from her His servant and messenger ʿIsa (ʿalayhi as-salam), one of the five great messengers of resolve (Ulu al-ʿAzm), ﴿she withdrew from her family to a place toward the east﴾, meaning she isolated herself from them and moved away from them, and went to the east of the Holy Mosque.

As-Suddi said: "Because of a menstruation that befell her." And it was said for other reasons. Abu Kudayna narrated from Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "The People of the Book were commanded to pray toward the House and to make pilgrimage to it, and nothing turned them away from it except the saying of your Lord: ﴿she withdrew from her family to a place toward the east﴾." He said: "Maryam went out to an eastward place, so they prayed toward the rising of the sun." Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it.

Ibn Jarir also said: Ishaq ibn Shahin narrated to us, Khalid ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, from Dawud, from ʿAmir, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "Indeed, I know, of all of Allah's creation, why the Christians took the east as a qibla: because of the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿she withdrew from her family to a place toward the east﴾, and they took the birthplace of ʿIsa as a qibla." (Tafsir al-Tabari 16/45).

Qatadah said: ﴿a place toward the east﴾ — distant, secluded.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: "She went with her pitcher to draw water."

Nawf al-Bikali said: "She took for herself a dwelling in which she worshipped." And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿So she took, apart from them, a screen﴾, meaning she concealed herself from them and hid herself, so Allah the Exalted sent to her Jibril (ʿalayhi as-salam), ﴿and he appeared to her as a man in every respect﴾, meaning in the form of a complete, perfect human being.

Mujahid, ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj, Wahb ibn Munabbih, and as-Suddi said, regarding His saying: ﴿We sent to her Our Spirit﴾, that it means Jibril (ʿalayhi as-salam).

And this which they said is the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, for Allah the Exalted said in another verse: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart that you may be of the warners﴾ [ash-Shuʿara': 193-194].

Abu Jaʿfar ar-Razi narrated from ar-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, from Abu al-ʿAliyah, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said: "Indeed, the spirit of ʿIsa (ʿalayhi as-salam) was among the spirits over which the covenant was taken in the time of Adam, and it is he who appeared to her as a man in every respect," i.e., the spirit of ʿIsa; so she conceived from the one who addressed her, and it entered into her mouth.

This is in extreme strangeness and rejection, and it seems to be from the Israʾiliyyat.

﴿She said, "Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you should be fearing of Allah"﴾, meaning: when the angel appeared to her in the form of a man, while she was in a secluded place, with a screen between her and her people, she feared him and thought he wanted her for herself, so she said: "I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are fearing Allah." That is, if you fear Allah. It is a reminder to him of Allah, and this is the prescribed way of repelling evil: to begin with the easiest and then the easier, so she first frightened him with Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to me, Abu Bakr narrated to us, from ʿAsim, who said: Abu Wail said—and he mentioned the story of Maryam—"She knew that the one who fears Allah has restraint, when she said: ﴿Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you should be fearing Allah.' He said, 'I am only the messenger of your Lord﴾", meaning: the angel said to her, responding to her and removing the fear she had for herself: "I am not what you suppose, but I am the messenger of your Lord," i.e., He sent me to you. It is said that when she mentioned the Most Merciful, Jibril trembled in fright and returned to his form and said: "I am only the messenger of your Lord, to bestow upon you a pure boy."

[Thus recited Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAla', one of the well-known reciters. The others recited: ﴿li-ahaba laki ghulaman zakiyyan﴾ (that I may bestow on you a pure boy).] Both recitations have a good aspect and a sound meaning, and each implies the other.

﴿She said, "How can I have a boy when no man has touched me and I have not been unchaste?"﴾ meaning: Maryam was amazed at this and said: How can I have a boy? That is, in what manner would this boy come to be from me, when I am not married and immorality is not conceivable from me? For this she said: ﴿no man has touched me and I have not been unchaste﴾. Al-baghiyy is the fornicator (al-zaniyah), and for this it came in a hadith that the earnings of the baghiyy are forbidden.

﴿He said, "Thus your Lord has said: It is easy for Me"﴾, meaning: the angel said to her, answering her question: "Indeed, Allah has said that He will bring forth from you a boy, though you have no husband and no immorality will occur from you, for He is capable of whatever He wills." For this He said: ﴿And that We may make him a sign for the people﴾, meaning: a proof and a sign for mankind of the power of their Creator and Originator, who varied His creation: He created their father Adam without male or female; He created Hawwa' from a male without a female; and He created the rest of the offspring from male and female. Except for ʿIsa, for He brought him forth from a female without a male. Thus the fourfold division was completed, which indicates the perfection of His power and the greatness of His dominion; there is no god but Him and no lord besides Him.

* *

His saying: ﴿And as a mercy from Us﴾, meaning: and We will make this boy a mercy from Allah, a prophet among the prophets, calling to the worship of Allah the Exalted and His monotheism, as Allah the Exalted said in another verse: ﴿When the angels said, "O Maryam, indeed Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, ʿIsa, son of Maryam, distinguished in this world and the Hereafter and among those brought near. He will speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity, and he is of the righteous"﴾ [Al ʿImran: 45-46], meaning: he will call to the worship of Allah his Lord in his cradle and in his maturity.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Rahim ibn Ibrahim (Duhaym) narrated to us, Marwan narrated to us, al-ʿAla' ibn al-Harith al-Kufi narrated to us, from Mujahid, who said: Maryam, upon her be peace, said: "When I was alone, ʿIsa would speak to me and converse with me while he was in my belly; and when I was with the people, he would glorify Allah and magnify Him in my belly."

* *

His saying: ﴿And it was a matter decreed﴾. It is possible that this is from the words of Jibril to Maryam, informing her that this is a matter predetermined in the knowledge, decree and will of Allah the Exalted. And it is possible that it is from the report of Allah the Exalted to His messenger Muhammad ﷺ, and that by this He alluded to the breathing into her private part, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Maryam, daughter of ʿImran, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into it of Our Spirit﴾ [at-Tahrim: 12], and He said: ﴿And she who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our Spirit﴾ [al-Anbiya': 91].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: "And it was a matter decreed," meaning: Allah has resolved upon this, so there is no escape from it. Ibn Jarir also chose this in his tafsir and did not report anything other than it. And Allah knows best.

She grew up among the Children of Israel in a great upbringing, and she was one of the worshipping, devout women, famous for great worship, devotion (tabattul) and diligence. She was under the guardianship of the husband of her sister—and it was said: her aunt—Zakariyya, the prophet of the Children of Israel at that time and their great one, to whom they would refer in their religion. Zakariyya saw from her such awesome marvels (karamat) that amazed him: ﴿Every time Zakariyya entered upon her in the prayer niche (mihrab), he found with her provision. He said, "O Maryam, from where is this for you?" She said, "It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account"﴾ [Al ʿImran: 37]. It is mentioned that he would find with her the fruit of winter in summer and the fruit of summer in winter, as was explained earlier in Surat Al ʿImran.

As-Suddi said: "Because of a menstruation that befell her." And it was said for other reasons. Abu Kudayna narrated from Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "The People of the Book were commanded to pray toward the House and to make pilgrimage to it, and nothing turned them away from it except the saying of your Lord: ﴿she withdrew from her family to a place toward the east﴾." Ibn Jarir also said: Ishaq ibn Shahin narrated to us, Khalid ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, from Dawud, from ʿAmir, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "Indeed, I know, of all of Allah's creation, why the Christians took the east as a qibla: because of the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿she withdrew from her family to a place toward the east﴾, and they took the birthplace of ʿIsa as a qibla." (Tafsir al-Tabari 16/45).

Qatadah said: ﴿a place toward the east﴾ — distant, secluded.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: "She went with her pitcher to draw water."

Nawf al-Bikali said: "She took for herself a dwelling in which she worshipped." And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿So she took, apart from them, a screen﴾, meaning she concealed herself from them and hid herself, so Allah the Exalted sent to her Jibril (ʿalayhi as-salam), ﴿and he appeared to her as a man in every respect﴾, meaning in the form of a complete, perfect human being.

Mujahid, ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj, Wahb ibn Munabbih, and as-Suddi said, regarding His saying: ﴿We sent to her Our Spirit﴾, that it means Jibril (ʿalayhi as-salam).

And this which they said is the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, for Allah the Exalted said in another verse: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart that you may be of the warners﴾ [ash-Shuʿara': 193-194].

Abu Jaʿfar ar-Razi narrated from ar-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, from Abu al-ʿAliyah, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said: "Indeed, the spirit of ʿIsa (ʿalayhi as-salam) was among the spirits over which the covenant was taken in the time of Adam, and it is he who appeared to her as a man in every respect," i.e., the spirit of ʿIsa; so she conceived from the one who addressed her, and it entered into her mouth.

This is in extreme strangeness and rejection, and it seems to be from the Israʾiliyyat.

﴿She said, "Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you should be fearing of Allah"﴾, meaning: when the angel appeared to her in the form of a man, while she was in a secluded place, with a screen between her and her people, she feared him and thought he wanted her for herself, so she said: "I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are fearing Allah." That is, if you fear Allah. It is a reminder to him of Allah, and this is the prescribed way of repelling evil: to begin with the easiest and then the easier, so she first frightened him with Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to me, Abu Bakr narrated to us, from ʿAsim, who said: Abu Wail said—and he mentioned the story of Maryam—"She knew that the one who fears Allah has restraint, when she said: ﴿Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you should be fearing Allah.' ﴿He said, "Thus your Lord has said: It is easy for Me"﴾, meaning: the angel said to her, answering her question: "Indeed, Allah has said that He will bring forth from you a boy, though you have no husband and no immorality will occur from you, for He is capable of whatever He wills." * *

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 19, verse 16–21:

When Allah the Exalted mentioned the story of Zakariyya (ʿalayhi as-salam), and that He brought forth from him, in his old age and his wife's barrenness, a pure, blessed, righteous son, He followed it with the mention of the story of Maryam in bringing forth her son ʿIsa, upon them both be peace, from her without a father. The two stories have a correspondence and a similarity (munasabah wa mushabahah). For this reason He mentioned them both in Surat Al ʿImran, here, and in Surat al-Anbiya', linking the two stories because of the closeness of their meaning, to show His servants His power and the greatness of His dominion, and that He is capable of whatever He wills. So He said: ﴿And mention in the Book Maryam﴾. She is Maryam bint ʿImran, of the lineage of Dawud (ʿalayhi as-salam), and she was from a pure, good household among the Children of Israel. Allah the Exalted has mentioned the story of her mother's giving birth to her in Surat Al ʿImran, and that her mother dedicated her as one freed (muharraran), meaning she would serve the Masjid of Bayt al-Maqdis, and they used to seek nearness to Allah through that: ﴿So her Lord accepted her with a good acceptance and caused her to grow in a good growth﴾ [Al ʿImran: 37]. She grew up among the Children of Israel in a great upbringing, and she was one of the worshipping, devout women, famous for great worship, devotion (tabattul) and diligence. She was under the guardianship of the husband of her sister—and it was said: her aunt—Zakariyya, the prophet of the Children of Israel at that time and their great one, to whom they would refer in their religion. Zakariyya saw from her such awesome marvels (karamat) that amazed him: ﴿Every time Zakariyya entered upon her in the prayer niche (mihrab), he found with her provision. He said, "O Maryam, from where is this for you?" She said, "It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account"﴾ [Al ʿImran: 37]. It is mentioned that he would find with her the fruit of winter in summer and the fruit of summer in winter, as was explained earlier in Surat Al ʿImran.

When Allah the Exalted—and to Him belong wisdom and conclusive proof—willed to bring forth from her His servant and messenger ʿIsa (ʿalayhi as-salam), one of the five great messengers of resolve (Ulu al-ʿAzm), ﴿she withdrew from her family to a place toward the east﴾, meaning she isolated herself from them and moved away from them, and went to the east of the Holy Mosque.

As-Suddi said: "Because of a menstruation that befell her." And it was said for other reasons. Abu Kudayna narrated from Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "The People of the Book were commanded to pray toward the House and to make pilgrimage to it, and nothing turned them away from it except the saying of your Lord: ﴿she withdrew from her family to a place toward the east﴾." He said: "Maryam went out to an eastward place, so they prayed toward the rising of the sun." Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it.

Ibn Jarir also said: Ishaq ibn Shahin narrated to us, Khalid ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, from Dawud, from ʿAmir, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "Indeed, I know, of all of Allah's creation, why the Christians took the east as a qibla: because of the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿she withdrew from her family to a place toward the east﴾, and they took the birthplace of ʿIsa as a qibla." (Tafsir al-Tabari 16/45).

Qatadah said: ﴿a place toward the east﴾ — distant, secluded.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: "She went with her pitcher to draw water."

Nawf al-Bikali said: "She took for herself a dwelling in which she worshipped." And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿So she took, apart from them, a screen﴾, meaning she concealed herself from them and hid herself, so Allah the Exalted sent to her Jibril (ʿalayhi as-salam), ﴿and he appeared to her as a man in every respect﴾, meaning in the form of a complete, perfect human being.

Mujahid, ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj, Wahb ibn Munabbih, and as-Suddi said, regarding His saying: ﴿We sent to her Our Spirit﴾, that it means Jibril (ʿalayhi as-salam).

And this which they said is the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, for Allah the Exalted said in another verse: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart that you may be of the warners﴾ [ash-Shuʿara': 193-194].

Abu Jaʿfar ar-Razi narrated from ar-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, from Abu al-ʿAliyah, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said: "Indeed, the spirit of ʿIsa (ʿalayhi as-salam) was among the spirits over which the covenant was taken in the time of Adam, and it is he who appeared to her as a man in every respect," i.e., the spirit of ʿIsa; so she conceived from the one who addressed her, and it entered into her mouth.

This is in extreme strangeness and rejection, and it seems to be from the Israʾiliyyat.

﴿She said, "Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you should be fearing of Allah"﴾, meaning: when the angel appeared to her in the form of a man, while she was in a secluded place, with a screen between her and her people, she feared him and thought he wanted her for herself, so she said: "I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are fearing Allah." That is, if you fear Allah. It is a reminder to him of Allah, and this is the prescribed way of repelling evil: to begin with the easiest and then the easier, so she first frightened him with Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to me, Abu Bakr narrated to us, from ʿAsim, who said: Abu Wail said—and he mentioned the story of Maryam—"She knew that the one who fears Allah has restraint, when she said: ﴿Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you should be fearing Allah.' He said, 'I am only the messenger of your Lord﴾", meaning: the angel said to her, responding to her and removing the fear she had for herself: "I am not what you suppose, but I am the messenger of your Lord," i.e., He sent me to you. It is said that when she mentioned the Most Merciful, Jibril trembled in fright and returned to his form and said: "I am only the messenger of your Lord, to bestow upon you a pure boy."

[Thus recited Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAla', one of the well-known reciters. The others recited: ﴿li-ahaba laki ghulaman zakiyyan﴾ (that I may bestow on you a pure boy).] Both recitations have a good aspect and a sound meaning, and each implies the other.

﴿She said, "How can I have a boy when no man has touched me and I have not been unchaste?"﴾ meaning: Maryam was amazed at this and said: How can I have a boy? That is, in what manner would this boy come to be from me, when I am not married and immorality is not conceivable from me? For this she said: ﴿no man has touched me and I have not been unchaste﴾. Al-baghiyy is the fornicator (al-zaniyah), and for this it came in a hadith that the earnings of the baghiyy are forbidden.

﴿He said, "Thus your Lord has said: It is easy for Me"﴾, meaning: the angel said to her, answering her question: "Indeed, Allah has said that He will bring forth from you a boy, though you have no husband and no immorality will occur from you, for He is capable of whatever He wills." For this He said: ﴿And that We may make him a sign for the people﴾, meaning: a proof and a sign for mankind of the power of their Creator and Originator, who varied His creation: He created their father Adam without male or female; He created Hawwa' from a male without a female; and He created the rest of the offspring from male and female. Except for ʿIsa, for He brought him forth from a female without a male. Thus the fourfold division was completed, which indicates the perfection of His power and the greatness of His dominion; there is no god but Him and no lord besides Him.

**Commentary of Ibn Kathir (*Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*) on Surah 19, verses 22–23:**

Allah, exalted is He, says, informing about Maryam (Mary), that when Jibril (Gabriel) said to her what Allah, exalted is He, had said, she submitted to the decree of Allah, exalted is He.[[In T: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic."]] Many scholars of the early generations (*salaf*) mentioned that the angel, who is Jibril, peace be upon him, at that moment blew into the opening of her garment (*jayb dir'iha*), and the breath descended until it entered the private part, and she conceived the child by the permission of Allah, exalted is He.

When she conceived him, she was distressed (*dhaqat dhar'an bihi*)[[In A: "bihima" (with both of them).]] and did not know what to say to the people, for she knew that the people would not believe her in what she informed them of. However, she disclosed her secret and mentioned her affair to her cousin, the wife of Zakariyya (Zechariah). That was because Zakariyya, peace be upon him, had asked Allah for a child, and he was granted that, so his wife conceived. Maryam entered upon her, and she rose to her and embraced her, and said: "Did you perceive, O Maryam, that I am pregnant?" Maryam said to her: "Did you also know that I am pregnant?" And she told her about her own affair and what had happened to her. They were a household of faith and affirmation. Then, after that, whenever the wife of Zakariyya faced Maryam, she would feel that what was in her womb was prostrating to what was in Maryam's womb, meaning: honoring it and humbling itself before it. Prostration (*sujud*) was legislated in their religion (*millah*) as a greeting, just as Ya'qub's parents and brothers prostrated to Yusuf, and just as Allah commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam, peace be upon him. But it was prohibited in this religion of ours, completing the glorification of the majesty of the Lord, exalted is He.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: It was recited to al-Harith ibn Miskin while I was listening, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim informed us, saying: Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said: It reached me that 'Isa ibn Maryam and Yahya ibn Zakariyya were cousins (*ibnay khalah*), and their conception occurred together at the same time. It reached me that the mother of Yahya said to Maryam: "Indeed I see that what is in my womb prostrates to what is in your womb." Malik said: I think that is due to the superiority of 'Isa, peace be upon him, because Allah made him able to revive the dead and to heal the blind (*al-akmah*) and the leper (*al-abras*).

Then the exegetes differed concerning the duration of the pregnancy of 'Isa, peace be upon him. The well-known view of the majority is that she carried him for nine months. Ikrimah said: eight months. He said: For this reason a child born at eight months does not survive.

Ibn Juraij said: Al-Mughira ibn Uthman ibn Abd Allah al-Thaqafi informed me that he heard Ibn Abbas, and he was asked about the pregnancy of Maryam, and he said: It was nothing more than that she conceived and gave birth.[[In A: "Ibn Utba" instead of "Ibn Uthman".]]

This is a strange report (*gharib*), and it seems he took it from the apparent meaning of the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿So she conceived him and withdrew with him to a remote place. Then the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree﴾. The particle *fa* (then) indicates sequence (*ta'qib*), but the sequence of each thing is according to its nature, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We created man from an extract of clay. Then We made him a drop [of fluid] in a firm place. Then We made the drop into a clinging clot, then We made the clot into a lump, then We made the lump into bones﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 12–14]. So this *fa* indicates sequence according to its own measure. And it is established in the two *Sahih* collections that between each of the two stages there are forty days.[[From the hadith of Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him; it will come at the commentary of verse 5 of Surah al-Hajj.]] And Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Do you not see that Allah sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green?﴾ [Al-Hajj: 63]. So the well-known and apparent view—and Allah is over all things competent—is that she carried him as women carry their children. For this reason, when the signs of pregnancy appeared upon her, and there was with her in the mosque a righteous man from among her relatives who served the Holy House (*Bayt al-Maqdis*) with her, called Yusuf the carpenter (*al-Najjar*), when he saw the heaviness and largeness of her belly, he denied that matter concerning her. Then what he knew of her innocence, purity, religion and worship restrained him, then he reflected on her situation, and her affair began to roam in his thoughts, and he could not turn it away from himself. So he forced himself to hint at her in speech, and said: "O Maryam, indeed I am going to ask you about a matter, so do not be hasty with me." She said: "And what is it?" He said: "Has a tree ever come into being without a seed? Or a crop without a sowing? Or a child without a father?" She said: "Yes"—she understood what he was pointing to—"As for your saying, 'Can there be a tree without a seed, or a crop without a sowing?' indeed Allah created the tree and the crop first, when He created them, without a seed or a sowing. 'And can there be a creation without a father?' Indeed Allah created Adam without a father and without a mother." So he believed her and accepted her condition.

When Maryam sensed from her people the accusation of immorality (*al-rayba*), she withdrew from them to a remote place (*makanan qasiyyan*), meaning: a place distant and far from them, so that they would not see her and she would not see them.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: When she conceived him and filled her jug (*qullatahā*)[[In A: "qalbaha" (her heart).]] and returned, the bleeding stopped for her, and there befell her what befalls a pregnant woman carrying a child of weakness, fatigue, and change of complexion, until her tongue was tied (*fatara lisanuha*). Nothing had entered upon a household what entered upon the family of Zakariyya. The story spread among the Children of Israel, and they said: "Its owner is only Yusuf," for there had been no one with her in the sanctuary (*kanisah*) except him. And she hid herself from the people and took a screen (*hijab*) from them, so no one saw her and she did not see anyone.

* *

His saying: ﴿Then the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree﴾ [meaning: so the labor pains compelled her and the birth pangs drove her to the trunk of a palm tree][[Addition from T and A.]] and it was a palm tree in the place to which she had withdrawn.

**Commentary of Ibn Kathir (*Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*) on Surah 19, verses 22–23:**

Allah, exalted is He, says, informing about Maryam (Mary), that when Jibril (Gabriel) said to her what Allah, exalted is He, had said, she submitted to the decree of Allah, exalted is He.[[In T: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic."]] Many scholars of the early generations (*salaf*) mentioned that the angel, who is Jibril, peace be upon him, at that moment blew into the opening of her garment (*jayb dir'iha*), and the breath descended until it entered the private part, and she conceived the child by the permission of Allah, exalted is He.

When she conceived him, she was distressed (*dhaqat dhar'an bihi*)[[In A: "bihima" (with both of them).]] and did not know what to say to the people, for she knew that the people would not believe her in what she informed them of. However, she disclosed her secret and mentioned her affair to her cousin, the wife of Zakariyya (Zechariah). That was because Zakariyya, peace be upon him, had asked Allah for a child, and he was granted that, so his wife conceived. Maryam entered upon her, and she rose to her and embraced her, and said: "Did you perceive, O Maryam, that I am pregnant?" Maryam said to her: "Did you also know that I am pregnant?" And she told her about her own affair and what had happened to her. They were a household of faith and affirmation. Then, after that, whenever the wife of Zakariyya faced Maryam, she would feel that what was in her womb was prostrating to what was in Maryam's womb, meaning: honoring it and humbling itself before it. Prostration (*sujud*) was legislated in their religion (*millah*) as a greeting, just as Ya'qub's parents and brothers prostrated to Yusuf, and just as Allah commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam, peace be upon him. But it was prohibited in this religion of ours, completing the glorification of the majesty of the Lord, exalted is He.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: It was recited to al-Harith ibn Miskin while I was listening, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim informed us, saying: Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said: It reached me that 'Isa ibn Maryam and Yahya ibn Zakariyya were cousins (*ibnay khalah*), and their conception occurred together at the same time. It reached me that the mother of Yahya said to Maryam: "Indeed I see that what is in my womb prostrates to what is in your womb." Malik said: I think that is due to the superiority of 'Isa, peace be upon him, because Allah made him able to revive the dead and to heal the blind (*al-akmah*) and the leper (*al-abras*).

Then the exegetes differed concerning the duration of the pregnancy of 'Isa, peace be upon him. The well-known view of the majority is that she carried him for nine months. Ikrimah said: eight months. He said: For this reason a child born at eight months does not survive.

Ibn Juraij said: Al-Mughira ibn Uthman ibn Abd Allah al-Thaqafi informed me that he heard Ibn Abbas, and he was asked about the pregnancy of Maryam, and he said: It was nothing more than that she conceived and gave birth.[[In A: "Ibn Utba" instead of "Ibn Uthman".]]

This is a strange report (*gharib*), and it seems he took it from the apparent meaning of the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿So she conceived him and withdrew with him to a remote place. Then the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree﴾. The particle *fa* (then) indicates sequence (*ta'qib*), but the sequence of each thing is according to its nature, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We created man from an extract of clay. Then We made him a drop [of fluid] in a firm place. Then We made the drop into a clinging clot, then We made the clot into a lump, then We made the lump into bones﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 12–14]. So this *fa* indicates sequence according to its own measure. And it is established in the two *Sahih* collections that between each of the two stages there are forty days.[[From the hadith of Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him; it will come at the commentary of verse 5 of Surah al-Hajj.]] And Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Do you not see that Allah sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green?﴾ [Al-Hajj: 63]. So the well-known and apparent view—and Allah is over all things competent—is that she carried him as women carry their children. For this reason, when the signs of pregnancy appeared upon her, and there was with her in the mosque a righteous man from among her relatives who served the Holy House (*Bayt al-Maqdis*) with her, called Yusuf the carpenter (*al-Najjar*), when he saw the heaviness and largeness of her belly, he denied that matter concerning her. Then what he knew of her innocence, purity, religion and worship restrained him, then he reflected on her situation, and her affair began to roam in his thoughts, and he could not turn it away from himself. So he forced himself to hint at her in speech, and said: "O Maryam, indeed I am going to ask you about a matter, so do not be hasty with me." She said: "And what is it?" He said: "Has a tree ever come into being without a seed? Or a crop without a sowing? Or a child without a father?" She said: "Yes"—she understood what he was pointing to—"As for your saying, 'Can there be a tree without a seed, or a crop without a sowing?' indeed Allah created the tree and the crop first, when He created them, without a seed or a sowing. 'And can there be a creation without a father?' Indeed Allah created Adam without a father and without a mother." So he believed her and accepted her condition.

When Maryam sensed from her people the accusation of immorality (*al-rayba*), she withdrew from them to a remote place (*makanan qasiyyan*), meaning: a place distant and far from them, so that they would not see her and she would not see them.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: When she conceived him and filled her jug (*qullatahā*)[[In A: "qalbaha" (her heart).]] and returned, the bleeding stopped for her, and there befell her what befalls a pregnant woman carrying a child of weakness, fatigue, and change of complexion, until her tongue was tied (*fatara lisanuha*). Nothing had entered upon a household what entered upon the family of Zakariyya. The story spread among the Children of Israel, and they said: "Its owner is only Yusuf," for there had been no one with her in the sanctuary (*kanisah*) except him. And she hid herself from the people and took a screen (*hijab*) from them, so no one saw her and she did not see anyone.

Some of them read ﴿مَنْ تَحْتَهَا﴾ (man taḥtahā) with the meaning of "alladhī taḥtahā" (the one beneath her). Others read ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ (min taḥtihā) as a preposition with a genitive ending.

The commentators differed over who is meant by this. Al-'Awfi and others related from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ ("Then he called to her from beneath her") is Jibril, and 'Isa did not speak until she brought him to her people. Likewise Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, 'Amr ibn Maymun, al-Suddi and Qatadah said: it is the angel Jibril, peace be upon him, meaning he called to her from the bottom of the valley.

Mujahid said: ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ refers to 'Isa ibn Maryam. Likewise 'Abd al-Razzaq related from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan said, "It is her son." This is also one of the two reports from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that it is her son. He said: "Did you not hear Allah say: ﴿فَأَشَارَتْ إِلَيْهِ﴾ (Then she pointed to him) [Maryam: 29]?" Ibn Zayd chose this view, as did Ibn Jarir in his tafsir. [Tafsir al-Tabari (16/52).]

* *

His saying: ﴿أَلا تَحْزَنِي﴾ (Do not grieve) means: he called to her saying, "Do not grieve." ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾ (Your Lord has placed beneath you a stream). Sufyan al-Thawri and Shu'bah related from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib: ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾, he said: "al-jadwal" (a small stream). Likewise 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: "al-sariyy is the river (al-nahr)." And 'Amr ibn Maymun said the same: "a river from which you drink."

Mujahid said: it is the river, in Syriac.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "al-sariyy is the small river, in Nabataean."

al-Dahhak said: it is the small river, in Syriac.

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: it is the small river.

Qatadah said: it is al-jadwal in the dialect of the people of the Hijaz.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: "al-sariyy is the rabi' of the water" (the flowing water).

al-Suddi said: it is the river, and Ibn Jarir chose this view. A hadith marfu' (traced to the Prophet) has also been narrated concerning this. al-Tabarani said:

Abu Shu'ayb al-Harrani narrated to us: Yahya ibn 'Abd Allah al-Babulti narrated to us: Ayyub ibn Nahik narrated to us: I heard 'Ikrimah, the freedman of Ibn 'Abbas, say: I heard Ibn 'Umar say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Indeed the sariyy about which Allah said to Maryam, ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾, is a river which Allah brought forth so that you might drink from it." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/346).] This hadith is extremely gharib (strange) from this route. And this Ayyub ibn Nahik is al-Hubuli. Abu Hatim al-Razi said of him: "Da'if" (weak). Abu Zur'ah said: "Munkar al-hadith" (his narrations are rejected). Abu al-Fath al-Azdi said: "Matruk al-hadith" (abandoned in narration).

Others said: the one meant by al-sariyy is 'Isa, peace be upon him. This was said by al-Hasan, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and Muhammad ibn 'Abbad ibn Ja'far. It is also one of the two reports from Qatadah, and the view of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam. The first view is more apparent; for this reason He said after it: ﴿وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ﴾ (And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree), meaning: and draw toward you the trunk of the palm tree. It was said: it was dry, related from Ibn 'Abbas. And it was said: it was fruit-bearing. Mujahid said: it was 'ajwah (a kind of date). al-Thawri said, from Abu Dawud Nufay' al-A'ma: it was sarafanah.

The apparent meaning is that it was a tree, but it was not in its season of fruiting; this is what Wahb ibn Munabbih said. For this reason He favoured her with it: He placed near her food and drink, and said: ﴿تُسَاقِطْ عَلَيْكِ رُطَبًا جَنِيًّا فَكُلِي وَاشْرَبِي وَقَرِّي عَيْنًا﴾ (It will drop upon you fresh ripe dates. So eat and drink and be comforted), meaning: be at ease in yourself. For this reason 'Amr ibn Maymun said: "There is nothing better for the woman in childbirth than dates and fresh dates," then he recited this noble verse.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us: Shaybān narrated to us: Maysur ibn Sa'id al-Tamimi narrated to us: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Amr al-Awza'i narrated to us, from 'Urwah ibn Ruwaym, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Honour your aunt, the palm tree, for it was created from the clay from which Adam, peace be upon him, was created, and there is no tree other than it that is pollinated." And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Feed your women the fresh dates when they give birth; if there are no fresh dates, then dates. And there is no tree more honoured by Allah than a tree beneath which Maryam bint 'Imran alighted."

This is an extremely munkar (rejected) hadith. Abu Ya'la related it from Shaybān with this chain. [Musnad Abi Ya'la (1/353). Abu Nu'aym related it in al-Hilyah (6/123) and Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil (6/431) through Maysur ibn Sa'd al-Tamimi, and Ibn 'Adi mentioned three defects for it: 1. Maysur alone narrated it from al-Awza'i, so it is munkar. 2. It is disconnected (munqati') between 'Urwah ibn Ruwaym and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. 3. Maysur ibn Sa'id is not known. I say: Ibn Hibban and al-'Uqayli declared him weak.]

They read his saying "tassāqaṭ" (ﾃ۔ﾃ・ﾃ・ﾃ・ﾃ・) with a shadda on the sin, and others without a shadda. Abu Nuhayk read ﴿تُسَاقِطْ عَلَيْكِ رُطَبًا جَنِيًّا﴾. Abu Ishaq related from al-Bara' that he read it "tusāqiṭ", meaning: the trunk. All of these are close in meaning.

* *

His saying: ﴿فَإِمَّا تَرَيِنَّ مِنَ الْبَشَرِ أَحَدًا﴾ (And if you see any human being) means: whenever you see anyone, ﴿فَقُولِي إِنِّي نَذَرْتُ لِلرَّحْمَنِ صَوْمًا فَلَنْ أُكَلِّمَ الْيَوْمَ إِنْسِيًّا﴾ (then say, "Indeed I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast, so I will not speak today to any human being"). The meaning of this saying is an indication by gesture to that, not that the intended meaning is a verbal utterance, so that it does not contradict ﴿فَلَنْ أُكَلِّمَ الْيَوْمَ إِنْسِيًّا﴾.

Anas ibn Malik said regarding His saying ﴿إِنِّي نَذَرْتُ لِلرَّحْمَنِ صَوْمًا﴾ that it means silence (ṣamtan). Likewise Ibn 'Abbas and al-Dahhak said. In a report from Anas: "ṣawman wa-ṣamtan" (fasting and silence). Likewise Qatadah and others said.

The meaning is that when they fasted in their law, food and speech were forbidden to them. This was explicitly stated by al-Suddi, Qatadah and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd.

Abu Ishaq related from Haritha, who said: I was with Ibn Mas'ud when two men came; one of them greeted him and the other did not. He said: "What is your matter?" His companions said: "He has sworn not to speak to people today." Then 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: "Speak to the people and greet them, for that was a woman who knew that no one would believe her that she had conceived without a husband." He meant by this Maryam, peace be upon her, so that it would be an excuse for her if she were questioned. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir related it, may Allah have mercy on them both.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: When 'Isa said to Maryam, ﴿أَلا تَحْزَنِي﴾ (Do not grieve), she said: "How should I not grieve when you are with me? I am neither a married woman nor a slave. So eat and drink and be comforted), meaning: be at ease in yourself. For this reason 'Amr ibn Maymun said: "There is nothing better for the woman in childbirth than dates and fresh dates," then he recited this noble verse.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us: Shaybān narrated to us: Maysur ibn Sa'id al-Tamimi narrated to us: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Amr al-Awza'i narrated to us, from 'Urwah ibn Ruwaym, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Honour your aunt, the palm tree, for it was created from the clay from which Adam, peace be upon him, was created, and there is no tree other than it that is pollinated." And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Feed your women the fresh dates when they give birth; if there are no fresh dates, then dates. And there is no tree more honoured by Allah than a tree beneath which Maryam bint 'Imran alighted."

This is an extremely munkar (rejected) hadith. Abu Ya'la related it from Shaybān with this chain. [Musnad Abi Ya'la (1/353). Abu Nu'aym related it in al-Hilyah (6/123) and Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil (6/431) through Maysur ibn Sa'd al-Tamimi, and Ibn 'Adi mentioned three defects for it: 1. Maysur alone narrated it from al-Awza'i, so it is munkar. 2. It is disconnected (munqati') between 'Urwah ibn Ruwaym and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. 3. Maysur ibn Sa'id is not known. I say: Ibn Hibban and al-'Uqayli declared him weak.]

They read his saying "tassāqaṭ" (ﾃ۔ﾃ・ﾃ・ﾃ・ﾃ・) with a shadda on the sin, and others without a shadda. Abu Nuhayk read ﴿تُسَاقِطْ عَلَيْكِ رُطَبًا جَنِيًّا﴾. Abu Ishaq related from al-Bara' that he read it "tusāqiṭ", meaning: the trunk. All of these are close in meaning.

* *

His saying: ﴿فَإِمَّا تَرَيِنَّ مِنَ الْبَشَرِ أَحَدًا﴾ (And if you see any human being) means: whenever you see anyone, ﴿فَقُولِي إِنِّي نَذَرْتُ لِلرَّحْمَنِ صَوْمًا فَلَنْ أُكَلِّمَ الْيَوْمَ إِنْسِيًّا﴾ (then say, "Indeed I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast, so I will not speak today to any human being"). The meaning of this saying is an indication by gesture to that, not that the intended meaning is a verbal utterance, so that it does not contradict ﴿فَلَنْ أُكَلِّمَ الْيَوْمَ إِنْسِيًّا﴾.

Anas ibn Malik said regarding His saying ﴿إِنِّي نَذَرْتُ لِلرَّحْمَنِ صَوْمًا﴾ that it means silence (ṣamtan). Likewise Ibn 'Abbas and al-Dahhak said. In a report from Anas: "ṣawman wa-ṣamtan" (fasting and silence). Likewise Qatadah and others said.

The meaning is that when they fasted in their law, food and speech were forbidden to them. This was explicitly stated by al-Suddi, Qatadah and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd.

Abu Ishaq related from Haritha, who said: I was with Ibn Mas'ud when two men came; one of them greeted him and the other did not. He said: "What is your matter?" His companions said: "He has sworn not to speak to people today." Then 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: "Speak to the people and greet them, for that was a woman who knew that no one would believe her that she had conceived without a husband." He meant by this Maryam, peace be upon her, so that it would be an excuse for her if she were questioned. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir related it, may Allah have mercy on them both.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: When 'Isa said to Maryam, ﴿أَلا تَحْزَنِي﴾ (Do not grieve), she said: "How should I not grieve when you are with me? I am neither a married woman nor a slave. What excuse will I have before the people? Would that I had died before this and been a thing forgotten and utterly forgotten." 'Isa said to her: "I will suffice you in speech": ﴿فَإِمَّا تَرَيِنَّ مِنَ الْبَشَرِ أَحَدًا فَقُولِي إِنِّي نَذَرْتُ لِلرَّحْمَنِ صَوْمًا فَلَنْ أُكَلِّمَ الْيَوْمَ إِنْسِيًّا﴾. He said: all of this is from the words of 'Isa to his mother. Wahb likewise said.

Some of them read ﴿مَنْ تَحْتَهَا﴾ (man taḥtahā) with the meaning of "alladhī taḥtahā" (the one beneath her). Others read ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ (min taḥtihā) as a preposition with a genitive ending.

The commentators differed over who is meant by this. Al-'Awfi and others related from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ ("Then he called to her from beneath her") is Jibril, and 'Isa did not speak until she brought him to her people. Likewise Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, 'Amr ibn Maymun, al-Suddi and Qatadah said: it is the angel Jibril, peace be upon him, meaning he called to her from the bottom of the valley.

Mujahid said: ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ refers to 'Isa ibn Maryam. Likewise 'Abd al-Razzaq related from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan said, "It is her son." This is also one of the two reports from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that it is her son. He said: "Did you not hear Allah say: ﴿فَأَشَارَتْ إِلَيْهِ﴾ (Then she pointed to him) [Maryam: 29]?" Ibn Zayd chose this view, as did Ibn Jarir in his tafsir. [Tafsir al-Tabari (16/52).]

* *

His saying: ﴿أَلا تَحْزَنِي﴾ (Do not grieve) means: he called to her saying, "Do not grieve." ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾ (Your Lord has placed beneath you a stream). Sufyan al-Thawri and Shu'bah related from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib: ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾, he said: "al-jadwal" (a small stream). Likewise 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: "al-sariyy is the river (al-nahr)." And 'Amr ibn Maymun said the same: "a river from which you drink."

Mujahid said: it is the river, in Syriac.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "al-sariyy is the small river, in Nabataean."

al-Dahhak said: it is the small river, in Syriac.

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: it is the small river.

Qatadah said: it is al-jadwal in the dialect of the people of the Hijaz.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: "al-sariyy is the rabi' of the water" (the flowing water).

al-Suddi said: it is the river, and Ibn Jarir chose this view. A hadith marfu' (traced to the Prophet) has also been narrated concerning this. al-Tabarani said:

Abu Shu'ayb al-Harrani narrated to us: Yahya ibn 'Abd Allah al-Babulti narrated to us: Ayyub ibn Nahik narrated to us: I heard 'Ikrimah, the freedman of Ibn 'Abbas, say: I heard Ibn 'Umar say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Indeed the sariyy about which Allah said to Maryam, ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾, is a river which Allah brought forth so that you might drink from it." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/346).] This hadith is extremely gharib (strange) from this route. And this Ayyub ibn Nahik is al-Hubuli. Abu Hatim al-Razi said of him: "Da'if" (weak). Abu Zur'ah said: "Munkar al-hadith" (his narrations are rejected). Abu al-Fath al-Azdi said: "Matruk al-hadith" (abandoned in narration).

Others said: the one meant by al-sariyy is 'Isa, peace be upon him. This was said by al-Hasan, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and Muhammad ibn 'Abbad ibn Ja'far. It is also one of the two reports from Qatadah, and the view of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam. The first view is more apparent; for this reason He said after it: ﴿وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ﴾ (And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree), meaning: and draw toward you the trunk of the palm tree. It was said: it was dry, related from Ibn 'Abbas. And it was said: it was fruit-bearing. Mujahid said: it was 'ajwah (a kind of date). al-Thawri said, from Abu Dawud Nufay' al-A'ma: it was sarafanah.

The apparent meaning is that it was a tree, but it was not in its season of fruiting; this is what Wahb ibn Munabbih said. For this reason He favoured her with it: He placed near her food and drink, and said: ﴿تُسَاقِطْ عَلَيْكِ رُطَبًا جَنِيًّا فَكُلِي وَاشْرَبِي وَقَرِّي عَيْنًا﴾ (It will drop upon you fresh ripe dates. So eat and drink and be comforted), meaning: be at ease in yourself. For this reason 'Amr ibn Maymun said: "There is nothing better for the woman in childbirth than dates and fresh dates," then he recited this noble verse.

And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Feed your women the fresh dates when they give birth; if there are no fresh dates, then dates. And there is no tree more honoured by Allah than a tree beneath which Maryam bint 'Imran alighted."

Abu Nu'aym related it in al-Hilyah (6/123) and Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil (6/431) through Maysur ibn Sa'd al-Tamimi, and Ibn 'Adi mentioned three defects for it: 1. Maysur alone narrated it from al-Awza'i, so it is munkar. 2. It is disconnected (munqati') between 'Urwah ibn Ruwaym and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. 3. Maysur ibn Sa'id is not known. I say: Ibn Hibban and al-'Uqayli declared him weak.]

His companions said: "He has sworn not to speak to people today."
