He meant by this Maryam, peace be upon her, so that it would be an excuse for her if she were questioned. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir related it, may Allah have mercy on them both.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: When 'Isa said to Maryam, ﴿أَلا تَحْزَنِي﴾ (Do not grieve), she said: "How should I not grieve when you are with me? I am neither a married woman nor a slave. What excuse will I have before the people? Would that I had died before this and been a thing forgotten and utterly forgotten." 'Isa said to her: "I will suffice you in speech": ﴿فَإِمَّا تَرَيِنَّ مِنَ الْبَشَرِ أَحَدًا فَقُولِي إِنِّي نَذَرْتُ لِلرَّحْمَنِ صَوْمًا فَلَنْ أُكَلِّمَ الْيَوْمَ إِنْسِيًّا﴾. He said: all of this is from the words of 'Isa to his mother. Wahb likewise said.

Ibn Kathir said, reporting from Allah, the Exalted, about Maryam (may Allah be pleased with her) when she was commanded to fast that day and not to speak to any human being: "Verily, she will be relieved of her affair and her proof will be established." So she submitted to the command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and surrendered to His decree. She took her child and ﴿brought him to her people, carrying him﴾. When they saw her in that state, they were greatly alarmed by her affair and found it extremely shocking, and they said: ﴿O Maryam, you have certainly come with a grave thing﴾. That is, a great matter. This was said by Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Suddi and others.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abi narrated to us, ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to us, Sayyar narrated to us, Jaʿfar ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Abu ʿImran al-Jawni narrated to us, from Nawf al-Bikali, who said: Her people went out seeking her, and she was from a household of prophethood and nobility. They could not find any trace of her, so they came upon a cowherd and said: "Did you see a girl of such-and-such description?" He said: "No, but last night I saw among my cows something I had never seen before from them." They said: "And what did you see?" He said: "I saw them prostrating towards this valley." ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad said: "I recall from Sayyar that he said: 'I saw a shining light.'" So they went in the direction he indicated to them, and Maryam met them. When she saw them, she sat down and held her son in her lap. They came and stood over her, and ﴿they said: "O Maryam, you have certainly come with a grave thing"﴾, a great matter. ﴿O sister of Harun﴾, that is, O one who resembles Harun in worship. ﴿Your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother an unchaste woman﴾, that is: you are from a good, pure household, known for righteousness, worship and asceticism, so how has this come from you?

ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah and al-Suddi said: She was addressed as ﴿O sister of Harun﴾, meaning the brother of Musa, since she was from his lineage, just as one says to a man of the Tamim tribe, "O brother of Tamim," and to a man of Mudar, "O brother of Mudar."

It was also said: She was attributed to a righteous man among them whose name was Harun, and she was compared to him in worship and asceticism.

Ibn Jarir reported from some of them that they likened her to a wicked man among them called Harun. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this from Saʿid ibn Jubayr.

Yet more strange than all of this is what Ibn Abi Hatim narrated.

ʿAli ibn al-Husayn al-Hisinjani narrated to us: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, al-Mufaddal ibn Fadalah narrated to us, Abu Sakhr narrated to us, from al-Qurazi, concerning the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿O sister of Harun﴾. He said: She was the full sister of Harun through both father and mother, and she was the sister of Musa, the brother of Harun, who followed Musa's trail, ﴿and he saw her from afar while they did not notice﴾ [al-Qasas: 11].

This statement is pure error. Allah has mentioned in His Book that He sent ʿIsa after the Messengers, which indicates that he was the last of the prophets to be sent, and that after him there was none but Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him. This is why it is established in Sahih al-Bukhari (authentic collection), from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "I am the most deserving of all people of the son of Maryam, though there is no prophet between me and him." If the matter were as Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi claimed, then he would not have come after the Messengers except Muhammad, and he would have come before Sulayman and Dawud. Allah has mentioned that Dawud came after Musa, peace be upon them both, in His saying: ﴿Have you not considered the eminent men of the Children of Israel after Musa, when they said to a prophet of theirs: "Send us a king, and we will fight in the way of Allah." He said: "Would you perhaps refrain from fighting if fighting were prescribed for you?" They said: "And why should we not fight in the way of Allah?"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 246], and he mentioned the story until he said: ﴿And Dawud killed Jalut﴾ [al-Baqarah: 251] and the verse.

What emboldened al-Qurazi to this claim is what is in the Torah after the departure of Musa and the Children of Israel from the sea and the drowning of Pharaoh and his people. It says that Maryam daughter of ʿImran, sister of the two prophets Musa and Harun, was beating the tambourine, and the women with her were glorifying Allah and thanking Him for what He had bestowed upon the Children of Israel. So al-Qurazi believed that this was the mother of ʿIsa. This is a grave blunder and a serious error. Rather, she was named after her (the other Maryam), and they used to name themselves after their prophets and righteous people, as Imam Ahmad said:

ʿAbd Allah ibn Idris narrated to us, I heard my father mention it, from Simak, from ʿAlqamah ibn Wa'il, from al-Mughirah ibn Shuʿbah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me to Najran. They said: "Have you seen what you recite: ﴿O sister of Harun﴾, and Musa was before ʿIsa by such-and-such years?" He said: I returned and mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "Did you not tell them that they used to name themselves after the prophets and righteous people before them?"

It was transmitted by Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasai alone, from the narration of ʿAbd Allah ibn Idris, from his father, from Simak, with this wording. al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih gharib (good, authentic, and rare); we do not know it except from the narration of Ibn Idris."

Ibn Jarir said: Yaʿqub narrated to me, Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Saʿid ibn Abi Sadaqah, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: I was informed that Kaʿb said: "Indeed His saying ﴿O sister of Harun﴾ does not refer to Harun the brother of Musa." He said: ʿAʾishah said to him: "You have lied." He said: "O Mother of the Believers, if the Prophet ﷺ said it, then he knows best and is most informed; otherwise I find that between them there are six hundred years." He said: So she fell silent. [Tafsir al-Tabari (16/58)] And there is some scrutiny regarding this chronology.

Ibn Jarir also said: Bishr narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah concerning His saying: ﴿O sister of Harun, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother an unchaste woman﴾. He said: She was from a family known for righteousness and not known for corruption, [and among people there are those known for righteousness who beget righteous offspring, and others known for corruption who beget corrupt offspring]. Harun was a reformer, beloved among his kin, and he was not Harun the brother of Musa, but another Harun. He said: It was mentioned to us that when he died, forty thousand people attended his funeral, all of them named Harun, from the Children of Israel.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then she pointed to him. They said: "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?"﴾, that is: when they doubted her affair and found her story shocking, and when they said to her what they said, hinting at slandering and accusing her of fornication, and she had been fasting that day, silent, she referred the speech to him and pointed to them towards his speaking and talking. They said, mocking her and thinking she was belittling them and toying with them: ﴿How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?﴾

Maymun ibn Mihran said: ﴿She pointed to him﴾, she said: "Speak to him." They said: "After what she has brought of calamity, she commands us to speak to one who is in the cradle, a child!"

al-Suddi said: When she pointed to him, they became angry and said: "Her mockery of us, when she commands us to speak to this infant, is harder on us than her fornication."

﴿They said: "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?"﴾, that is: one who is present in his cradle during his infancy and childhood, how can he speak? He said: ﴿Indeed I am the servant of Allah﴾. The first thing he spoke was to glorify the sublime majesty of his Lord, the Exalted, and to declare Allah free from having a son, and to affirm for himself servitude to his Lord.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet﴾, it is a clearing of his mother from the immorality attributed to her.

Nawf al-Bikali said: When they said to his mother what they said, he was nursing from her breast. He pulled the breast from his mouth, leaned on his left side and said: ﴿Indeed I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet﴾, up to His saying: ﴿as long as I remain alive﴾.

Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit al-Bunani, said: He raised his index finger above his shoulder while saying: ﴿Indeed I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet﴾, the verse.

ʿIkrimah said: ﴿He has given me the Scripture﴾, that is: He decreed that He would give me the Scripture among what He decreed.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa narrated to us, Yahya ibn Saʿid narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Ziyad, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: ʿIsa ibn Maryam had studied the Injil and mastered it while in his mother's womb. That is His saying: ﴿Indeed I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet﴾.

Yahya ibn Saʿid al-ʿAttar al-Himsi: matruk (abandoned, i.e., rejected by hadith scholars as unreliable).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And He made me blessed wherever I am﴾, Mujahid, ʿAmr ibn Qays and al-Thawri said: "He made me a teacher of good." In another narration from Mujahid: "a benefactor."

Ibn Jarir said: Sulayman ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbar narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Khunays al-Makhzumi narrated to us, I heard Wuhayb ibn al-Ward, client of the Banu Makhzum, say: A scholar met another scholar who was above him in knowledge, and he said to him: "May Allah have mercy on you, what is it that I should openly practise of my deeds?" He said: "Enjoining good and forbidding evil, for it is the religion of Allah with which He sent His prophets to His servants. The jurists have agreed upon the words of Allah: ﴿And He made me blessed wherever I am﴾." It was said: "What is its blessing?" He said: "Enjoining good and forbidding evil, wherever it may be."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And He enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I remain alive﴾, it is like His saying to Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty﴾ [al-Hijr: 99].

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim said, from Malik ibn Anas, concerning His saying: ﴿And He enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I remain alive﴾: "He informed him of what would occur of His command until he dies," and he did not affirm it for the people of qadar (divine decree, here meaning the Qadariyyah, who denied predestination).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And dutiful to my mother﴾, that is: and He commanded me to be dutiful to my mother. Many historians from the People of the Book and others have also mentioned that Constantine gathered them in a great assembly, from among their three well-known councils. The body of bishops numbered 2,170 bishops, and they differed about ʿIsa ibn Maryam, peace be upon him, in sharply conflicting ways. Each group said a saying about him: one hundred said one thing, seventy said another, fifty said something else, and one hundred and sixty said something. No more than three hundred and eight of them agreed upon a single position. They agreed upon one statement and insisted on it. The king inclined toward them, and he was a philosopher. He advanced them, supported them, and expelled everyone else. So they set up for him the great covenant, which was in fact a great betrayal, and they wrote for him books of laws, legislated for him matters, and invented many innovations, and they distorted and changed the religion of the Messiah. Then he built for them great churches throughout his entire kingdom: the lands of al-Sham, al-Jazirah, and Rome. The number of churches in his days came to nearly twelve thousand churches [[In A: "twelve," which is an error; the correct form is as in the original.]]. His mother Helena built al-Qumamah [the Church of the Holy Sepulchre] on the place where the crucified one was crucified, whom the Jews and Christians claim to be the Messiah. They have lied. Rather, Allah raised him to the heaven.

* *

Allah said: ﴿So woe to those who disbelieved, from the scene of a great day﴾. This is a threat and a severe warning to those who lied against Allah, fabricated, and claimed that He has a son. However, Allah the Exalted gave them respite until the Day of Resurrection, and delayed them out of forbearance and confidence in His power over them, for He is the One who does not hasten against those who disobey Him. As it came in the two Sahihs: "Indeed Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer, until when He seizes him, He does not let him go." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿And such is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are wrongdoing. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe﴾ [Hud: 102]. Also in the two Sahihs, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "No one is more patient with harm he hears from Allah. They attribute to Him a son, yet He provides for them and grants them well-being." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 6099 and Sahih Muslim no. 2804.] Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And how many a city did I give respite while it was wrongdoing; then I seized it, and to Me is the final return﴾ [al-Hajj: 48]. And He said: ﴿And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them until a Day when eyes will stare fixedly﴾ [Ibrahim: 42]. For this reason He said here: ﴿So woe to those who disbelieved, from the scene of a great day﴾, that is, the Day of Resurrection. It has also come in the authentic hadith agreed upon for its authenticity, from ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever testifies that there is no god but Allah, alone, without partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger, and that ʿIsa is the servant of Allah [and His messenger] [[Added from F, A, and al-Bukhari and Muslim.]], and His word which He cast to Maryam and a spirit from Him, and that Paradise is true and the Fire is true, Allah will admit him into Paradise according to what deeds he had." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 3435 and Sahih Muslim no. 29.]

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah Maryam (19), verses 38–40:

God, exalted is He, says, informing about the disbelievers [on the Day of Resurrection]¹ that they will be the most hearing and the most seeing of all things, as He said: ﴿If only you could see when the criminals hang their heads before their Lord, saying: "Our Lord, we have seen and we have heard, so send us back that we may do righteous deeds; indeed we are now certain."﴾ (32:12). That is, they will say this at a time when it will not benefit them nor avail them anything. Had this been said before witnessing the punishment, it would have benefited them and saved them from the punishment of God. Therefore He said: ﴿How well they will hear and see²﴾, that is, how much they will hear and see ﴿on the Day they come to Us³﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection. ﴿But the wrongdoers today⁴﴾, that is, in the world, ﴿are in clear error⁵﴾, meaning they neither hear, nor see, nor understand. So when they are called to guidance, they do not accept it, and they become obedient when that will no longer benefit them.

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret⁶﴾, that is, warn all creatures of the Day of Regret, ﴿when the matter will be decided⁷﴾, that is, when a separation is made between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire, and each enters what he has come to, abiding in it forever. ﴿And they⁸﴾, that is, today, ﴿are heedless⁹﴾ of what they were warned about, ﴿and they do not believe¹⁰﴾, that is, they do not affirm it.

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id [al-Khudri]¹¹, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, Death will be brought in the form of a white-speckled ram, and it will be stopped between Paradise and the Fire. Then it will be said: 'O people of Paradise, do you recognize this?' They will crane their necks, look, and say: 'Yes, this is Death.' Then it will be said: 'O people of the Fire, do you recognize this?' They will crane their necks, look, and say: 'Yes, this is Death.' Then it will be commanded regarding it, and it will be slaughtered." He said: "And it will be said: 'O people of Paradise, eternity without death! And O people of the Fire, eternity without death!'" He said: Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited: ﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will be decided, while they are heedless¹²﴾, and he indicated with his hand, and said: "The people of this world are in the heedlessness of this world."

Thus did Imam Ahmad narrate it. It was also related by al-Bukhari and Muslim in their Sahihs, from the hadith of al-A'mash, with the same chain¹³, and their wording is similar to this. This hadith was also narrated by al-Hasan ibn 'Arafa: Aspat ibn Muhammad narrated to me, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, raised to the Prophet, similar to it. In Sunan Ibn Majah and elsewhere, it is narrated through Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, similar to it¹⁴. It is also in the two Sahihs from Ibn 'Umar¹⁵. Ibn Jurayj narrated it, saying: Ibn 'Abbas said: and he mentioned something similar to it from his side. He also narrated from his father that he heard 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr say in his stories: Death will be brought as if it were an animal, and it will be slaughtered while the people look on¹⁶.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Abu al-Za'ra', from 'Abd Allah [ibn Mas'ud], in a story he mentioned: No soul will remain except that it looks at a house in Paradise and a house in the Fire, and that is the Day of Regret. The people of the Fire will see the house that God had prepared for them had they believed, and it will be said to them: "Had you believed and done righteous deeds, this would have been yours, which you see in Paradise." Then regret will seize them. He said: And the people of Paradise will see the house that is in the Fire, and it will be said: "Had God not favored you..."¹⁷

And al-Suddi said, from Ziyad, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding His saying: ﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will be decided﴾: When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, Death will be brought in the form of a white-speckled ram until it is stopped between Paradise and the Fire. Then a caller will call: "O people of Paradise, this is the Death that used to cause people to die in the world." No one among the people of 'Illiyyin¹⁸ or in the lowest rank of Paradise will remain except that he looks at it. Then it will be called: "O people of the Fire, this is the Death that used to cause people to die in the world." No one in the shallow part of the Fire or in the lowest level of Hell will remain except that he looks at it. Then it will be slaughtered between Paradise and the Fire. Then it will be called: "O people of Paradise, it is eternity forever and ever! And O people of the Fire, it is eternity forever and ever!" The people of Paradise will rejoice with such joy that, had anyone died of joy, they would die; and the people of the Fire will wail with such a wail that, had anyone died of wailing, they would die. That is His saying: ﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will be decided﴾, meaning: when Death is slaughtered¹⁹. Ibn Abi Hatim related it in his Tafsir.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret﴾: It is among the names of the Day of Resurrection; God magnified it and warned His servants of it.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said regarding His saying: ﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret﴾: It is the Day of Resurrection, and he recited: ﴿Lest a soul should say: "Alas for my regret over what I neglected concerning God"﴾ (39:56).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, We inherit the earth and whoever is on it, and to Us they will be returned﴾: God, exalted is He, informs that He is the Creator, the Owner, the Disposer of affairs, and that all creation will perish while He remains, exalted and sanctified is He. No one claims ownership or authority; rather, He is the Inheritor of all His creation, the One who remains after them, the Judge over them. So no soul will be wronged in anything, not even the weight of a gnat's wing or an atom's weight.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Hudbah ibn Khalid al-Qaysi mentioned to us: Hazm ibn Abi Hazm al-Quta'i narrated to us, saying: 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz wrote to 'Abd al-Hamid ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, the governor of Kufa: "To proceed: God decreed for His creation, when He created them, death, and made their final return to Him. He said, in what He sent down in His truthful Book, which He preserved by His knowledge and whose witnesses among His creation were His angels: that He inherits the earth and whoever is on it, and to Him they will be returned."

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, We inherit the earth and whoever is on it, and to Us they will be returned﴾: God, exalted is He, informs that He is the Creator, the Owner, the Disposer of affairs, and that all creation will perish while He remains, exalted and sanctified is He. No one claims ownership or authority; rather, He is the Inheritor of all His creation, the One who remains after them, the Judge over them. So no soul will be wronged in anything, not even the weight of a gnat's wing or an atom's weight.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Hudbah ibn Khalid al-Qaysi mentioned to us: Hazm ibn Abi Hazm al-Quta'i narrated to us, saying: 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz wrote to 'Abd al-Hamid ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, the governor of Kufa: "To proceed: God decreed for His creation, when He created them, death, and made their final return to Him. He said, in what He sent down in His truthful Book, which He preserved by His knowledge and whose witnesses among His creation were His angels: that He inherits the earth and whoever is on it, and to Him they will be returned."

Allah says, reporting the reply of Abu Ibrahim (Ibrahim's father) to what his son had called him to: he said, ﴿Do you reject my gods, O Ibrahim?﴾ Meaning: if you do not wish to worship them and do not approve of them, then desist from reviling them, insulting them and finding fault with them. For if you do not desist from that, I will take retribution against you, abuse you and revile you. This is his saying: ﴿Surely I will stone you﴾. This was related by Ibn 'Abbas, al-Suddi, Ibn Juraij, al-Dahhak and others.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and leave me for a long time﴾: Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: it means for a long time (dahr).

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: a long period of time. Al-Suddi said: ﴿and leave me for a long time﴾ means: forever.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah and al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and leave me for a long time﴾ means: safe and sound, before some punishment from me befalls you. Likewise said al-Dahhak, Qatadah, 'Atiyyah al-Jadali and Abu Malik, and others, and Ibn Jarir chose this view.

Then Ibrahim said to his father: ﴿Peace be upon you.﴾ This is as Allah said describing the believers: ﴿And when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace"﴾ [al-Furqan: 63], and Allah said: ﴿And when they hear vain talk, they turn away from it and say, "To us our deeds and to you your deeds. Peace be upon you. We do not seek the ignorant."﴾ [al-Qasas: 55].

The meaning of Ibrahim's saying to his father, ﴿Peace be upon you﴾, is: as for me, no harm or injury from me will reach you, and this is out of respect for fatherhood. ﴿I will ask my Lord to forgive you﴾, i.e., but I will ask Allah, the Exalted, on your behalf to guide you and forgive your sin. ﴿Indeed He has always been gracious to me﴾: Ibn 'Abbas and others said: kind (laṭīf), i.e., in that He guided me to worship Him and to sincerity toward Him. Mujahid, Qatadah and others said: ﴿Indeed He has always been gracious to me﴾ — he said: He has accustomed me to being answered. [and] al-Suddi said: "al-Ḥafiy" is the one who cares about his affair.

Ibrahim asked forgiveness for his father for a long time, even after he migrated to al-Sham, and after he built the Sacred House, and after Isma'il and Ishaq were born to him, peace be upon them, in his saying: ﴿Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers on the day the reckoning is established﴾ [Ibrahim: 41].

The Muslims also asked forgiveness for their relatives and family members among the polytheists at the beginning of Islam, following the example of Ibrahim the Friend (khalil) in this, until Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿There is certainly for you an excellent example in Ibrahim and those with him, when they said to their people, "Indeed, we are free of you and what you worship besides Allah. We have rejected you, and there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever until you believe in Allah alone," except for the saying of Ibrahim to his father, "I will surely ask forgiveness for you, but I have not [power to get] for you anything from Allah."﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 4] — meaning, except in this statement, so do not follow him in it. Then Allah the Exalted made clear that Ibrahim desisted from that and turned back from it, so Allah the Exalted said: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Hellfire﴾ [at-Tawbah: 113–114].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And I will leave you and what you invoke besides Allah, and I will call upon my Lord﴾: i.e., I will avoid you and disassociate myself from you and from your gods which you worship besides Allah. ﴿And I will call upon my Lord﴾: i.e., I will worship my Lord alone, with no partner for Him. ﴿Perhaps I will not be in my supplication to my Lord unfortunate.﴾ This "perhaps" (ʿasā) here is binding without doubt, for he, peace be upon him, was the chief of the prophets after Muhammad (ﷺ).

He says: When the Friend (al-Khalil) withdrew from his father and his people for the sake of Allah, Allah replaced him with those who were better than them, and He bestowed upon him Ishaq (Isaac) and Ya'qub (Jacob), meaning his son and the son of Ishaq, as He said in the other verse: ﴿And to Ya'qub as a grandson﴾ [al-Anbiya': 72], and He said: ﴿And after Ishaq, Ya'qub﴾ [Hud: 71].

There is no disagreement that Ishaq is the father of Ya'qub, and this is the explicit statement of the Qur'an in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿Or were you witnesses when death approached Ya'qub, when he said to his sons, "What will you worship after me?" They said, "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Ibrahim and Isma'il and Ishaq, one God, and we are Muslims [submitting] to Him."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 133]. For this reason, here He mentioned only Ishaq and Ya'qub, meaning: We made for him offspring and descendants who were prophets, with whom Allah gladdened his eye during his lifetime. For this reason He said: ﴿And each We made a prophet﴾. Had Ya'qub not been made a prophet during the lifetime of Ibrahim, he would not have been singled out, and his son Yusuf would have been mentioned, for he too is a prophet, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said in the hadith whose authenticity is agreed upon, when he was asked about the best of people, and he said: "Yusuf, the Prophet of Allah, son of Ya'qub, the Prophet of Allah, son of Ishaq, the Prophet of Allah, son of Ibrahim, the Friend of Allah." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3374) and Sahih Muslim no. (2378).] And in another wording: "Verily the noble, son of the noble, son of the noble, son of the noble: Yusuf ibn Ya'qub ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4688).]

* *

Ibn Jarir said: He only said ﴿'Aliyy﴾ because all the religions and creeds praise them and extol them, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all.

When Allah the Exalted mentioned Ibrahim the Friend (khalil) and praised him, He followed with mention of the one who spoke with Him (al-Kalim), saying: ﴿And mention in the Book Musa. Indeed, he was chosen (mukhlasan)﴾. Some of them read it with a kasra on the lam, from ikhlas (sincerity) in worship.

Al-Thawri said, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Rufay', from Abu Lubabah: The disciples (al-Hawariyyun) said: "O Spirit of Allah, tell us about the one who is sincere (mukhlis) for Allah." He said: "The one who acts for Allah, and does not love that people praise him."

Others read it with a fatha on the lam, meaning that he was chosen (mustafa), as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿I have chosen you above the people﴾ [al-A'raf: 144].

﴿And he was a messenger, a prophet﴾: both qualities were combined for him, for he was among the great messengers, the five possessors of resolve (ulu al-'azm), who are: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa and Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them and upon all the prophets.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We called him from the right side of the mount﴾, i.e., the mountain ﴿al-Ayman﴾, meaning: from its right side relative to Musa, when he went seeking a burning brand from that fire, and saw it blazing, so he headed toward it, and found it on the right side of the mount, at the edge of the valley. Allah the Exalted spoke to him, called him, brought him near, and conversed with him in private (naja).

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Yahya—that is al-Qattan—narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿And We brought him near as a confidant﴾: He said: "He was brought near until he heard the scratching of the pen."

Mujahid, Abu al-'Aliyah and others said likewise, meaning the scratching of the pen writing the Torah.

Al-Suddi said: ﴿And We brought him near as a confidant﴾: "He was taken up into the heavens and spoken to," and similarly from Mujahid.

Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And We brought him near as a confidant﴾: "He was saved by his truthfulness (naja bi-sidqihi)."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abd al-Jabbar ibn Asim narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Salamah al-Harrani narrated to us, from Abu al-Wassil, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Amr ibn Ma'd Yakrib, who said: When Allah brought Musa near as a confidant at Tur Sinai, He said: "O Musa, if I create for you a grateful heart, a remembering tongue, and a wife who helps you toward good, I will not withhold from you any good thing, and whoever I withhold this from, I will not open for him any good."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We gave him, out of Our mercy, his brother Harun as a prophet﴾: i.e., We answered his request and his intercession for his brother, and made him a prophet, as He said in another verse: ﴿And my brother Harun, he is more eloquent in tongue than I, so send him with me as a helper to confirm me; indeed I fear that they will deny me﴾ [al-Qasas: 34]; and He said: ﴿You have been granted your request, O Musa﴾ [Ta-Ha: 36]; and He said: ﴿So send to Harun. And they have a charge against me, so I fear they will kill me﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 13–14]. For this reason some of the predecessors (salaf) said: "No one has interceded for another in this world with an intercession greater than the intercession of Musa for Harun that he should be a prophet." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We gave him, out of Our mercy, his brother Harun as a prophet﴾.

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub narrated to us, Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Dawud, from Ikrimah, who said: Ibn Abbas said regarding His saying: ﴿And We gave him, out of Our mercy, his brother Harun as a prophet﴾: "Harun was older than Musa, but the meaning is: He granted him his prophethood."

Ibn Abi Hatim also transmitted it in suspended form (mu'allaq), from Ya'qub, who is Ibn Ibrahim al-Dawraqi, with the same chain.

[Source note: Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (no. 33) and Muslim in his Sahih (no. 59) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Since these are the characteristics of the hypocrites, adopting their opposites is among the characteristics of the believers. For this reason Allah praised His servant and messenger Isma'il for truthfulness in promises. Likewise, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was also true to his promises; he never promised anyone something without fulfilling it for them. He praised Abu al-As ibn al-Rabi', the husband of his daughter Zaynab, saying: "He spoke to me and was truthful with me, and he promised me and fulfilled it for me." [Source note: Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (no. 3729) and Muslim in his Sahih (no. 2449) from the hadith of al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, may Allah be pleased with him.] When the Prophet (ﷺ) died, the caliph Abu Bakr al-Siddiq said: "Whoever had a promise or a debt owed to him by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), let him come to me and I will fulfill it for him." Jabir ibn Abdullah came to him and said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said: 'If the wealth of Bahrain comes, I will give you such and such and such,' meaning a handful of both his hands." When the wealth of Bahrain came, al-Siddiq ordered Jabir, so he scooped with both hands from the wealth. Then he ordered him to count it, and it was five hundred dirhams, so he gave him double that along with it. [Source note: Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (no. 2683) and Muslim in his Sahih (no. 2314).]

It has been established in Sahih Muslim [its wording in Muslim (no. 2276): "Indeed Allah chose Kinanah from the descendants of Isma'il, and chose Quraysh from Kinanah," and Allah knows best] that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah chose Isma'il from the descendants of Ibrahim..." and he mentioned the rest of the hadith. This confirms what we have said.

* *

We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you, and the best outcome is for righteousness﴾ [Ta-Ha: 132]. Allah, the Exalted, also said: ﴿O you who believe, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are angels, harsh and severe...﴾ [al-Tahrim: 6], meaning: command them to what is good, forbid them from what is evil, and do not leave them neglected, lest the Fire consume them on the Day of Resurrection.

Truthfulness in promises is among the praiseworthy qualities, just as breaking promises is among the blameworthy qualities. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do? It is greatly hateful in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do﴾ [al-Saff: 2-3]. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The sign of the hypocrite is three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted he betrays." [Source note: Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (no. 33) and Muslim in his Sahih (no. 59) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Since these are the characteristics of the hypocrites, adopting their opposites is among the characteristics of the believers. For this reason Allah praised His servant and messenger Isma'il for truthfulness in promises. Likewise, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was also true to his promises; he never promised anyone something without fulfilling it for them. He praised Abu al-As ibn al-Rabi', the husband of his daughter Zaynab, saying: "He spoke to me and was truthful with me, and he promised me and fulfilled it for me." [Source note: Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (no. 3729) and Muslim in his Sahih (no. 2449) from the hadith of al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, may Allah be pleased with him.] When the Prophet (ﷺ) died, the caliph Abu Bakr al-Siddiq said: "Whoever had a promise or a debt owed to him by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), let him come to me and I will fulfill it for him." Jabir ibn Abdullah came to him and said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said: 'If the wealth of Bahrain comes, I will give you such and such and such,' meaning a handful of both his hands." When the wealth of Bahrain came, al-Siddiq ordered Jabir, so he scooped with both hands from the wealth. Then he ordered him to count it, and it was five hundred dirhams, so he gave him double that along with it. [Source note: Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (no. 2683) and Muslim in his Sahih (no. 2314).]

* *

His saying ﴿and he was a messenger and a prophet﴾ indicates the excellence of Isma'il over his brother Ishaq, because Ishaq was only described as a prophet (nabi), whereas Isma'il was described as both a prophet and a messenger (rasul). It has been established in Sahih Muslim [its wording in Muslim (no. 2276): "Indeed Allah chose Kinanah from the descendants of Isma'il, and chose Quraysh from Kinanah," and Allah knows best] that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah chose Isma'il from the descendants of Ibrahim..." and he mentioned the rest of the hadith. This confirms what we have said.

* *

His saying ﴿and he used to enjoin his family to prayer and zakah, and he was pleasing to his Lord﴾: This is also a beautiful praise and a praiseworthy attribute and a commendable quality, since he was persistent in obeying his Lord and commanded his family to do so as well. Just as Allah, the Exalted, said to His Messenger: ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family and be steadfast in it. We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you, and the best outcome is for righteousness﴾ [Ta-Ha: 132]. Allah, the Exalted, also said: ﴿O you who believe, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are angels, harsh and severe...﴾ [al-Tahrim: 6], meaning: command them to what is good, forbid them from what is evil, and do not leave them neglected, lest the Fire consume them on the Day of Resurrection.

It has come in a hadith from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy on a man who gets up at night and prays, and wakes his wife; if she refuses, he sprinkles water on her face. May Allah have mercy on a woman who gets up at night and prays, and wakes her husband; if he refuses, she sprinkles water on his face." Narrated by Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah. [Source note: Sunan Abi Dawud (no. 1450) and Sunan Ibn Majah (no. 1336).]

And from Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "When a man wakes up at night and wakes his wife, and the two of them pray two rak'ahs, they are recorded among the men and women who remember Allah much." Narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Majah, and the wording is his. [Source note: Sunan Abi Dawud (no. 1451), al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Nasa'i (no. 11406), and Sunan Ibn Majah (no. 1335).]

This is the mention of Idris, peace be upon him, with praise for him: that he was truthful (*siddiq*), a prophet, and that Allah raised him to a lofty station. It has already been mentioned in the Sahih that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by him on the night of the Isra' (Night Journey) while he was in the fourth heaven.

Ibn Jarir [al-Tabari] narrated here a strange and remarkable report. He said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la told me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Jarir ibn Hazim informed me, from Sulayman al-A'mash, from Shamir ibn 'Atiyyah, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, who said: Ibn 'Abbas asked Ka'b, while I was present, "What is the meaning of Allah's saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, concerning Idris: ﴿And We raised him to a lofty station﴾?" Ka'b said: "As for Idris, Allah revealed to him that I raise for you every day the like of the deeds of all the children of Adam. So he desired to increase his deeds. A close friend of his from among the angels came to him and said: 'Allah has revealed to me such and such, so intercede for me with the Angel of Death, that he may delay me so I can increase my deeds.' So the angel carried him between his wings until he ascended with him to the heaven. When he was in the fourth heaven, the Angel of Death met them descending, and he (the angel) spoke to the Angel of Death about what Idris had asked of him. The Angel of Death said: 'Where is Idris?' He said: 'He is here, on my back.' The Angel of Death said: 'How wondrous! I was sent and it was said to me: "Take the soul of Idris in the fourth heaven."' So I kept saying: 'How can I take his soul in the fourth heaven when he is on the earth?' Then he took his soul there. That is the meaning of Allah's saying: ﴿And We raised him to a lofty station﴾."

This is among the reports of Ka'b al-Ahbar and of the Isra'iliyyat (narratives of Israelite origin), and some of it is objectionable, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from another route, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he asked Ka'b, and he mentioned something similar to what preceded, except that he said to that angel: "Would you ask Him, that is, the Angel of Death, how much of my term remains, so that I may increase in deeds," and he mentioned the rest of it. In it: when he asked him about what remained of his term, he (the Angel of Death) said: "I do not know until I look." Then he looked and said: "You are asking me about a man of whom only the blink of an eye remains of his life." So the angel looked under his wing at Idris, and behold, he had been taken, peace be upon him, while he did not perceive it.

Then he narrated it from another route from Ibn 'Abbas: that Idris was a tailor, and he would not thrust a needle without saying "Glory be to Allah," so he would be in the evening when evening came, and there was no one on earth with better deeds than him. He mentioned the rest of it like the previous report, or similar to it.

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿And We raised him to a lofty station﴾: "Idris was raised and did not die, just as 'Isa was raised."

Sufyan said, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿And We raised him to a lofty station﴾: "He was raised to the fourth heaven."

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And We raised him to a lofty station﴾: "He was raised to the sixth heaven and died there." Likewise said al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim.

Al-Hasan and others said, concerning His saying: ﴿And We raised him to a lofty station﴾: "It is Paradise."

This is the mention of Idris, peace be upon him, with praise for him: that he was truthful (*siddiq*), a prophet, and that Allah raised him to a lofty station. It has already been mentioned in the Sahih that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by him on the night of the Isra' (Night Journey) while he was in the fourth heaven.

Ibn Jarir [al-Tabari] narrated here a strange and remarkable report. He said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la told me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Jarir ibn Hazim informed me, from Sulayman al-A'mash, from Shamir ibn 'Atiyyah, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, who said: Ibn 'Abbas asked Ka'b, while I was present, "What is the meaning of Allah's saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, concerning Idris: ﴿And We raised him to a lofty station﴾?" Ka'b said: "As for Idris, Allah revealed to him that I raise for you every day the like of the deeds of all the children of Adam. So he desired to increase his deeds. A close friend of his from among the angels came to him and said: 'Allah has revealed to me such and such, so intercede for me with the Angel of Death, that he may delay me so I can increase my deeds.' So the angel carried him between his wings until he ascended with him to the heaven. When he was in the fourth heaven, the Angel of Death met them descending, and he (the angel) spoke to the Angel of Death about what Idris had asked of him. The Angel of Death said: 'Where is Idris?' He said: 'He is here, on my back.' The Angel of Death said: 'How wondrous! I was sent and it was said to me: "Take the soul of Idris in the fourth heaven."' So I kept saying: 'How can I take his soul in the fourth heaven when he is on the earth?' Then he took his soul there. That is the meaning of Allah's saying: ﴿And We raised him to a lofty station﴾."

This is among the reports of Ka'b al-Ahbar and of the Isra'iliyyat (narratives of Israelite origin), and some of it is objectionable, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from another route, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he asked Ka'b, and he mentioned something similar to what preceded, except that he said to that angel: "Would you ask Him, that is, the Angel of Death, how much of my term remains, so that I may increase in deeds," and he mentioned the rest of it. In it: when he asked him about what remained of his term, he (the Angel of Death) said: "I do not know until I look." Then he looked and said: "You are asking me about a man of whom only the blink of an eye remains of his life." So the angel looked under his wing at Idris, and behold, he had been taken, peace be upon him, while he did not perceive it.

Then he narrated it from another route from Ibn 'Abbas: that Idris was a tailor, and he would not thrust a needle without saying "Glory be to Allah," so he would be in the evening when evening came, and there was no one on earth with better deeds than him. He mentioned the rest of it like the previous report, or similar to it.

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿And We raised him to a lofty station﴾: "Idris was raised and did not die, just as 'Isa was raised."

Sufyan said, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿And We raised him to a lofty station﴾: "He was raised to the fourth heaven."

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And We raised him to a lofty station﴾: "He was raised to the sixth heaven and died there." Likewise said al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim.

Al-Hasan and others said, concerning His saying: ﴿And We raised him to a lofty station﴾: "It is Paradise."

Allah the Exalted says: "These are the prophets" — and the intended meaning is not only those mentioned in this surah, but the whole category of prophets, peace be upon them. He digressed from naming individuals to speaking of the category — "those upon whom Allah bestowed favour from among the prophets, of the offspring of Adam" — and so on.

Al-Suddi and Ibn Jarir (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "Those intended by 'of the offspring of Adam' are Idris; those intended by 'of the offspring of those whom We carried with Nuh' are Ibrahim; those intended by 'of the offspring of Ibrahim' are Ishaq, Ya'qub and Isma'il; those intended by 'of the offspring of Isra'il' are Musa, Harun, Zakariyya, Yahya and 'Isa ibn Maryam."

Ibn Jarir said: "For this reason He distinguished their lineages, although Adam encompasses all of them, because among them is one who is not a descendant of those who were with Nuh in the ark, namely Idris, for he is the grandfather of Nuh."

I (Ibn Kathir) say: This is the more apparent view, that Idris is in the direct line of descent of Nuh, peace be upon them both. It has also been said that he was one of the prophets of the Children of Israel, based on the hadith of the Night Journey (Isra'), where he said in greeting to the Prophet ﷺ: "Welcome to the righteous prophet and the righteous brother," and did not say "the righteous son," as Adam and Ibrahim said, peace be upon them both.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus narrated to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Ibn Lahi'a informed me, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, that Idris was earlier than Nuh. Allah sent him to his people, and he commanded them to say, "There is no god but Allah," and to act as they wished, but they refused, so Allah the Mighty and Majestic destroyed them.

[Among what supports that the intended meaning of this verse is the category of prophets is that it is like His saying in Surah al-An'am: "And that was Our argument which We gave to Ibrahim against his people; We raise by degrees whom We will. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing. And We gave him Ishaq and Ya'qub, each of whom We guided; and Nuh We guided before; and among his descendants Dawud, Sulayman, Ayyub, Yusuf, Musa and Harun. Thus do We reward the doers of good. And Zakariyya, Yahya, 'Isa and Ilyas, all of the righteous. And Isma'il, al-Yasa', Yunus and Lut, and each We preferred over the worlds. And from their forefathers, their descendants and their brothers; and We chose them and guided them to a straight path." Up to His saying: "Those are the ones whom Allah guided, so follow their guidance. Say: I do not ask you for it any payment; it is not but a reminder to the worlds" [al-An'am 83-90]. And He the Exalted said: "Of them are those We have related to you, and of them are those We have not related to you" [Ghafir: 78]. In Sahih al-Bukhari, from Mujahid: he asked Ibn 'Abbas, "Is there a prostration in Sad?" He said, "Yes," then recited this verse: "Those are the ones whom Allah guided, so follow their guidance," and said, "Your Prophet is among those whom he was commanded to follow," and said, "And he (Dawud) is among them," meaning Dawud. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4807.]]

And Allah the Exalted said in this noble verse: "When the verses of the Most Merciful are recited to them, they fall down prostrating and weeping." That is: when they hear the speech of Allah, which contains His proofs, evidences and demonstrations, they prostrate to their Lord in humility, submission, praise and gratitude for the great blessings they are in.

"Bukiyy" is the plural of "baki" (weeping one). For this reason, the scholars agreed on the legislation of prostration here, following their example and adhering to their way.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Abu Ma'mar, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, recited Surah Maryam, prostrated, and said: "This is the prostration; so where is the weeping?" meaning the crying.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it, and "Abu Ma'mar" has dropped from its chain in what I have seen [Tafsir al-Tabari 16/73]. And Allah knows best.

When the Most High mentioned the party of the blessed, namely the prophets, peace be upon them, and those who followed them among those who uphold Allah's limits and commands, who fulfil Allah's obligations and abstain from what He forbids, He mentioned that ﴿after them there succeeded a generation﴾, meaning other generations, ﴿who neglected the prayer﴾. If they neglected it, they are even more negligent of the other obligations, because it is the pillar and foundation of the religion and the best of the deeds of the servants. ﴿And followed their appetites﴾, and devoted themselves to the desires and pleasures of this world, and were content with the life of this world and found rest in it. ﴿So they will meet Ghayy﴾, meaning loss, on the Day of Resurrection.

Scholars have differed over what is meant here by neglecting the prayer. Some said that it means abandoning it entirely. This was said by Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, Ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and al-Suddi, and Ibn Jarir chose this view. For this reason, some of the early scholars (al-salaf), the later scholars (al-khalaf), and the imams went to the view, as is well known from Imam Ahmad, and as is one opinion from al-Shafi'i, that one who abandons the prayer is a disbeliever (kafir). This is based on the hadith: "Between a servant and shirk is the abandoning of the prayer,"[[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (82), from the hadith of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him.]] and the other hadith: "The covenant between us and them is the prayer; whoever abandons it has disbelieved."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (2621), and al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (1/231), from the hadith of Buraydah ibn al-Husayb, may Allah be pleased with him. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih gharib hadith."]] This is not the place to expand on this issue.

Al-Awza'i said, from Musa ibn Sulayman, from al-Qasim ibn Mukhaymirah, concerning His saying ﴿So there succeeded after them a generation who neglected the prayer﴾: "They only neglected the appointed times. Had it been abandonment, it would have been disbelief."

Waki' said, from al-Mas'udi, from al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman and al-Hasan ibn Sa'd, from Ibn Mas'ud, that it was said to him: "Allah mentions the prayer frequently in the Qur'an: ﴿who are heedless of their prayer﴾, ﴿who are constant in their prayer﴾, and ﴿who guard their prayers﴾." Ibn Mas'ud said: "[It refers to] its appointed times." They said: "We did not understand that except as referring to abandonment." He said: "That is disbelief."

Masruq said: "No one who guards the five prayers will be recorded among the heedless. Excessiveness in them leads to destruction, and their excessiveness is neglecting them beyond their time."

Al-Awza'i said, from Ibrahim ibn Yazid,[[In A: "Zayd".]] that Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz recited: ﴿So there succeeded after them a generation who neglected the prayer and followed their appetites, so they will meet Ghayy﴾, then said: "Their neglect was not abandoning it, but neglecting its time."

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid: ﴿So there succeeded after them a generation who neglected the prayer and followed their appetites﴾, he said: "This is at the coming of the Hour and the passing of the righteous of the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ, when they will leap upon one another in the alleys." Ibn Jurayj similarly narrated from Mujahid the same.

Jabir al-Ju'fi narrated from Mujahid, Ikrimah, and Ata' ibn Abi Rabah that they are from this Ummah, meaning at the end of time.

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Harith narrated to me, al-Hasan al-Ashyab narrated to us, Shurayk narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from Mujahid: ﴿So there succeeded after them a generation who neglected the prayer and followed their appetites﴾, he said: "They are in this Ummah, mounting one another like cattle and donkeys in the roads, not fearing Allah in the heaven, nor being shy of people on earth."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti narrated to us, Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri' narrated to us, Haywah narrated to us, Bashir ibn Abi Amr al-Khawlani narrated to us, that al-Walid ibn Qays narrated to him that he heard Abu Sa'id al-Khudri say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "After sixty years there will be a generation who neglected the prayer and followed their appetites, so they will meet Ghayy. Then there will be a generation who recite the Qur'an but it does not go beyond their throats. The Qur'an is recited by three: a believer, a hypocrite, and a wicked person." Bashir said: I said to al-Walid: "What are these three?" He said: "The believer believes in it, the hypocrite disbelieves in it, and the wicked person eats by it."

Ahmad narrated it likewise from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri'.[[In F, A: "al-Maqbari".]] with this chain.[[Al-Musnad (3/38).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: My father narrated to me, Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Isa ibn Yunus informed us, Ubayd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Mawhab[[In F, A: "Ibn Wahb".]] narrated to us, from Malik, from [[In F: "Ibn".]] Abu al-Rijal, that Aishah used to send some things as charity to the People of the Suffah, and she would say: "Do not give any of it to a Berber man or a Berber woman, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'They are the successors (khalf) whom Allah the Most High described: ﴿So there succeeded after them a generation who neglected the prayer﴾.'" This is a gharib hadith.[[Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (2/244) through the route of al-Hasan ibn Ali from Ibrahim ibn Musa with this chain. He said: "This hadith has a sahih chain, but they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not narrate it." al-Dhahabi responded to him saying: "Ubayd Allah is disputed as to his reliability, I do not know Malik (in this route), and it is then disconnected (munqati')."]]

He also said: My father narrated to me, Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Dahhak narrated to us, al-Walid narrated to us, Hariz[[In T, F, A: "Ibn Jarir".]] narrated to us, from a shaykh from the people of Madinah, that he heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi say concerning His saying ﴿So there succeeded after them a generation﴾ to the end of the verse: "They are the people of the West (al-gharb),[[In T: "al-qura"; in A: "al-maghrib".]] who rule, and they are the worst of rulers."

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: "By Allah, I find the description of the hypocrites in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: drinkers of desires, abandoners of prayers, playful with the cubes, sleeping through the night prayers, negligent in the morning, abandoners of the Friday gatherings." He said: Then he recited this verse: ﴿So there succeeded after them a generation who neglected the prayer and followed their appetites, so they will meet Ghayy﴾.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "They left the mosques empty and clung to idleness (al-day'at)."

Abu al-Ashhab al-Utaridi said: Allah the Most High revealed to Dawud: "O Dawud, warn and caution your companions against eating (in pursuit of) desires, for the hearts attached to the desires of this world have their intellects veiled from Me. The least I would do to a servant of Mine who prefers one of his desires over Me is to deprive him of obeying Me."

Imam Ahmad said: Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, Abu al-Samh[[Addition from F, A and the Musnad.]] al-Tamimi narrated to us, from Abu Qabil,[[In A: "from Ibn Qunbul".]] that he heard Uqbah[[In T: "Abd Allah".]] ibn Amir say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I fear for my Ummah two things: the Qur'an and the milk. As for the milk, they will pursue the lush pastures (al-rif) and follow their appetites and abandon the prayers. As for the Qur'an, the hypocrites will learn it and argue with it against the believers."[[Al-Musnad (4/156). What is meant by "milk," as al-Harbi said: "I think he meant they distance themselves from the cities and from congregational prayer, seeking places with milk in pastures and deserts."]]

Ibn Lahi'ah narrated it from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Ibn[[In T: "Abi".]] Lahi'ah: Abu Qabil narrated to us, from Uqbah, with it, as a marfu' hadith similar to this, narrated by him alone.[[Al-Musnad (4/146).]]

* *

As for His saying ﴿so they will meet Ghayy﴾: Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Ghayy﴾ means loss. Qatadah said: evil.

Sufyan al-Thawri, Shu'bah, and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud: ﴿Ghayy﴾, he said: "A valley in Hell, deep in its bottom and foul in its taste."

Al-A'mash said, from Ziyad, from Abu Iyad, concerning His saying ﴿Ghayy﴾: "A valley in Hell of pus and blood."

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Abbas ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Ziyad ibn Zayyan narrated to us, Sharqi ibn Qatami narrated to us, from Luqman ibn Amir al-Khuza'i, who said: I came to Abu Umamah Sudayy ibn Ajlan al-Bahili and said: "Narrate to us a hadith you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said: He called for food, then said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If a rock the weight of ten awqiyah were hurled from the brink of Hell, it would not reach its bottom in fifty autumns, and then it would arrive at Ghayy and Athām." I said: "What are Ghayy and Athām?" He said: "Two wells at the bottom of Hell, from which flows the pus of the people of the Fire, and they are the two that Allah mentioned in His Book: ﴿They neglected the prayer and followed their appetites, so they will meet Ghayy﴾, and His saying in al-Furqan: ﴿and they do not commit adultery, and whoever does that will meet Athām﴾."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (16/75).]] This is a gharib hadith, and its marfu' form is munkar.

* *

As for His saying ﴿except for one who repents, believes, and does righteous work﴾: meaning, except for one who returns from neglecting the prayers and following appetites, for Allah accepts his repentance, makes his end good, and makes him among the inheritors of the Garden of Bliss. Therefore He said: ﴿those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged at all﴾. This is because repentance erases what came before it. In another hadith: "The one who repents from sin is like one who has no sin."[[It has come from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Sa'id al-Ansari, and Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them all. The best of them is the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan, no. (4250), but it has a break in its chain (inqita').]] Therefore these repentant ones will not have any of their deeds diminished, nor will they be repaid for what they did before it so that something of what they did after it is reduced for them, because that is wiped out, left as forgotten, and goes for nothing, out of the generosity of the Generous and the forbearance of the Forbearing.

This exception here is like His saying in Surah al-Furqan: ﴿And those who do not call upon another god besides Allah, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit adultery, and whoever does that will meet a penalty. The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in humiliation. Except one who repents, believes, and does righteous work; for those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds, and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Furqan: 68–70].

When the Most High mentioned the party of the blessed, namely the prophets, peace be upon them, and those who followed them among those who uphold Allah's limits and commands, who fulfil Allah's obligations and abstain from what He forbids, He mentioned that ﴿after them there succeeded a generation﴾, meaning other generations, ﴿who neglected the prayer﴾. If they neglected it, they are even more negligent of the other obligations, because it is the pillar and foundation of the religion and the best of the deeds of the servants. ﴿And followed their appetites﴾, and devoted themselves to the desires and pleasures of this world, and were content with the life of this world and found rest in it. ﴿So they will meet Ghayy﴾, meaning loss, on the Day of Resurrection.

Scholars have differed over what is meant here by neglecting the prayer. Some said that it means abandoning it entirely. This was said by Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, Ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and al-Suddi, and Ibn Jarir chose this view. For this reason, some of the early scholars (al-salaf), the later scholars (al-khalaf), and the imams went to the view, as is well known from Imam Ahmad, and as is one opinion from al-Shafi'i, that one who abandons the prayer is a disbeliever (kafir). This is based on the hadith: "Between a servant and shirk is the abandoning of the prayer,"[[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (82), from the hadith of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him.]] and the other hadith: "The covenant between us and them is the prayer; whoever abandons it has disbelieved."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (2621), and al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (1/231), from the hadith of Buraydah ibn al-Husayb, may Allah be pleased with him. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih gharib hadith."]] This is not the place to expand on this issue.

Al-Awza'i said, from Musa ibn Sulayman, from al-Qasim ibn Mukhaymirah, concerning His saying ﴿So there succeeded after them a generation who neglected the prayer﴾: "They only neglected the appointed times. Had it been abandonment, it would have been disbelief."

Waki' said, from al-Mas'udi, from al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman and al-Hasan ibn Sa'd, from Ibn Mas'ud, that it was said to him: "Allah mentions the prayer frequently in the Qur'an: ﴿who are heedless of their prayer﴾, ﴿who are constant in their prayer﴾, and ﴿who guard their prayers﴾." Ibn Mas'ud said: "[It refers to] its appointed times." They said: "We did not understand that except as referring to abandonment." He said: "That is disbelief."

Masruq said: "No one who guards the five prayers will be recorded among the heedless. Excessiveness in them leads to destruction, and their excessiveness is neglecting them beyond their time."

Al-Awza'i said, from Ibrahim ibn Yazid,[[In A: "Zayd".]] that Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz recited: ﴿So there succeeded after them a generation who neglected the prayer and followed their appetites, so they will meet Ghayy﴾, then said: "Their neglect was not abandoning it, but neglecting its time."

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid: ﴿So there succeeded after them a generation who neglected the prayer and followed their appetites﴾, he said: "This is at the coming of the Hour and the passing of the righteous of the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ, when they will leap upon one another in the alleys." Ibn Jurayj similarly narrated from Mujahid the same.

Jabir al-Ju'fi narrated from Mujahid, Ikrimah, and Ata' ibn Abi Rabah that they are from this Ummah, meaning at the end of time.

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Harith narrated to me, al-Hasan al-Ashyab narrated to us, Shurayk narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from Mujahid: ﴿So there succeeded after them a generation who neglected the prayer and followed their appetites﴾, he said: "They are in this Ummah, mounting one another like cattle and donkeys in the roads, not fearing Allah in the heaven, nor being shy of people on earth."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti narrated to us, Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri' narrated to us, Haywah narrated to us, Bashir ibn Abi Amr al-Khawlani narrated to us, that al-Walid ibn Qays narrated to him that he heard Abu Sa'id al-Khudri say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "After sixty years there will be a generation who neglected the prayer and followed their appetites, so they will meet Ghayy. Then there will be a generation who recite the Qur'an but it does not go beyond their throats. The Qur'an is recited by three: a believer, a hypocrite, and a wicked person." Bashir said: I said to al-Walid: "What are these three?" He said: "The believer believes in it, the hypocrite disbelieves in it, and the wicked person eats by it."

Ahmad narrated it likewise from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri'.[[In F, A: "al-Maqbari".]] with this chain.[[Al-Musnad (3/38).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: My father narrated to me, Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Isa ibn Yunus informed us, Ubayd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Mawhab[[In F, A: "Ibn Wahb".]] narrated to us, from Malik, from [[In F: "Ibn".]] Abu al-Rijal, that Aishah used to send some things as charity to the People of the Suffah, and she would say: "Do not give any of it to a Berber man or a Berber woman, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'They are the successors (khalf) whom Allah the Most High described: ﴿So there succeeded after them a generation who neglected the prayer﴾.'" This is a gharib hadith.[[Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (2/244) through the route of al-Hasan ibn Ali from Ibrahim ibn Musa with this chain. He said: "This hadith has a sahih chain, but they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not narrate it." al-Dhahabi responded to him saying: "Ubayd Allah is disputed as to his reliability, I do not know Malik (in this route), and it is then disconnected (munqati')."]]

He also said: My father narrated to me, Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Dahhak narrated to us, al-Walid narrated to us, Hariz[[In T, F, A: "Ibn Jarir".]] narrated to us, from a shaykh from the people of Madinah, that he heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi say concerning His saying ﴿So there succeeded after them a generation﴾ to the end of the verse: "They are the people of the West (al-gharb),[[In T: "al-qura"; in A: "al-maghrib".]] who rule, and they are the worst of rulers."

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: "By Allah, I find the description of the hypocrites in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: drinkers of desires, abandoners of prayers, playful with the cubes, sleeping through the night prayers, negligent in the morning, abandoners of the Friday gatherings." He said: Then he recited this verse: ﴿So there succeeded after them a generation who neglected the prayer and followed their appetites, so they will meet Ghayy﴾.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "They left the mosques empty and clung to idleness (al-day'at)."

Abu al-Ashhab al-Utaridi said: Allah the Most High revealed to Dawud: "O Dawud, warn and caution your companions against eating (in pursuit of) desires, for the hearts attached to the desires of this world have their intellects veiled from Me. The least I would do to a servant of Mine who prefers one of his desires over Me is to deprive him of obeying Me."

Imam Ahmad said: Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, Abu al-Samh[[Addition from F, A and the Musnad.]] al-Tamimi narrated to us, from Abu Qabil,[[In A: "from Ibn Qunbul".]] that he heard Uqbah[[In T: "Abd Allah".]] ibn Amir say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I fear for my Ummah two things: the Qur'an and the milk. As for the milk, they will pursue the lush pastures (al-rif) and follow their appetites and abandon the prayers. As for the Qur'an, the hypocrites will learn it and argue with it against the believers."[[Al-Musnad (4/156). What is meant by "milk," as al-Harbi said: "I think he meant they distance themselves from the cities and from congregational prayer, seeking places with milk in pastures and deserts."]]

Ibn Lahi'ah narrated it from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Ibn[[In T: "Abi".]] Lahi'ah: Abu Qabil narrated to us, from Uqbah, with it, as a marfu' hadith similar to this, narrated by him alone.[[Al-Musnad (4/146).]]

* *

As for His saying ﴿so they will meet Ghayy﴾: Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Ghayy﴾ means loss. Qatadah said: evil.

Sufyan al-Thawri, Shu'bah, and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud: ﴿Ghayy﴾, he said: "A valley in Hell, deep in its bottom and foul in its taste."

Al-A'mash said, from Ziyad, from Abu Iyad, concerning His saying ﴿Ghayy﴾: "A valley in Hell of pus and blood."

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Abbas ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Ziyad ibn Zayyan narrated to us, Sharqi ibn Qatami narrated to us, from Luqman ibn Amir al-Khuza'i, who said: I came to Abu Umamah Sudayy ibn Ajlan al-Bahili and said: "Narrate to us a hadith you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said: He called for food, then said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If a rock the weight of ten awqiyah were hurled from the brink of Hell, it would not reach its bottom in fifty autumns, and then it would arrive at Ghayy and Athām." I said: "What are Ghayy and Athām?" He said: "Two wells at the bottom of Hell, from which flows the pus of the people of the Fire, and they are the two that Allah mentioned in His Book: ﴿They neglected the prayer and followed their appetites, so they will meet Ghayy﴾, and His saying in al-Furqan: ﴿and they do not commit adultery, and whoever does that will meet Athām﴾."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (16/75).]] This is a gharib hadith, and its marfu' form is munkar.

* *

As for His saying ﴿except for one who repents, believes, and does righteous work﴾: meaning, except for one who returns from neglecting the prayers and following appetites, for Allah accepts his repentance, makes his end good, and makes him among the inheritors of the Garden of Bliss. Therefore He said: ﴿those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged at all﴾. This is because repentance erases what came before it. In another hadith: "The one who repents from sin is like one who has no sin."[[It has come from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Sa'id al-Ansari, and Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them all. The best of them is the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan, no. (4250), but it has a break in its chain (inqita').]] Therefore these repentant ones will not have any of their deeds diminished, nor will they be repaid for what they did before it so that something of what they did after it is reduced for them, because that is wiped out, left as forgotten, and goes for nothing, out of the generosity of the Generous and the forbearance of the Forbearing.

This exception here is like His saying in Surah al-Furqan: ﴿And those who do not call upon another god besides Allah, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit adultery, and whoever does that will meet a penalty. The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in humiliation. Except one who repents, believes, and does righteous work; for those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds, and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Furqan: 68–70].

The Most High says: "The gardens which the repentant from their sins enter" are ﴿Gardens of Eden﴾, that is, of abode, ﴿which the Most Merciful has promised His servants﴾ in the unseen, that is, they are from the unseen which they believe in, and have not seen. This is because of the intensity of their certainty and the strength of their faith.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, His promise is ever coming to pass﴾ is an emphasis on the occurrence of that, its establishment and its being fixed. For Allah does not break the appointment, nor change it, like His saying: ﴿His promise is ever fulfilled﴾ [Al-Muzzammil: 18], that is, it is certainly going to happen.

* *

And His saying here: ﴿ma'tiyyan (coming to pass)﴾ means that the servants will arrive at it, and will come to it. Some have said: ﴿ma'tiyyan﴾ means ﴿ati(yan)﴾ (arriving), because everything that comes to you, you have come to it, as the Arabs say: "Fifty years came upon me," and "I came upon fifty years," both with the same meaning.

His saying: ﴿They will not hear therein any idle talk﴾, that is, in these gardens there is no worthless, vain speech that has no meaning, as may be found in this world.

* *

His saying: ﴿except the word "Peace"﴾ is an exceptive clause of disconnection (istithna' munqati'), like His saying: ﴿They will not hear therein any idle talk or sinful speech, except the word "Peace, peace"﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah: 25–26].

* *

His saying: ﴿And they will have their provision therein morning and evening﴾, that is, in the likeness of the times of morning and evening, not that there is night or day there; rather they are periods that alternate, and they know their passing by lights and radiance, as Imam Ahmad said:

Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first group to enter Paradise will have their faces like the moon on the night of the full moon. They will not spit therein, nor blow their noses, nor defecate. Their vessels and combs will be of gold and silver, their censers will be of aloes-wood, their sweat will be musk, and each one of them will have two wives, through whose shins the marrow can be seen beyond the flesh, from their beauty. There is no disagreement among them nor hatred; their hearts are as one heart, and they glorify Allah morning and evening."

Both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it in their Sahihs through the narration of Ma'mar.

Imam Ahmad said: Ya'qub narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, Al-Harith ibn Fudayl al-Ansari narrated to me, from Mahmud ibn Labid al-Ansari, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The martyrs are at the bank of a river at the gate of Paradise, in a green dome; their provision comes out to them from Paradise morning and evening." Ahmad alone narrated it through this chain.

Al-Dahhak said, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And they will have their provision therein morning and evening﴾: "It is the measures of night and day."

Ibn Jarir said: Ali ibn Sahm narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, who said: I asked Zuhayr ibn Muhammad about the saying of Allah the Most High: ﴿And they will have their provision therein morning and evening﴾, and he said: "There is no night in Paradise; they are always in light, and for them there is the measure of night and day: they know the measure of night by the lowering of the veils and the closing of the doors, and they know the measure of day by the raising of the veils and the opening of the doors."

By this same chain, from al-Walid ibn Muslim, from Khulayd, from al-Hasan al-Basri, who mentioned the gates of Paradise and said: "Gates whose outside is seen from within; they speak and are spoken to; they understand: 'Open,' 'Close,' and it does so."

Qatadah said regarding His saying: ﴿And they will have their provision therein morning and evening﴾: "In it there are two times: morning and evening; there is no night nor day there, but only brightness and light."

Mujahid said: "There is no morning nor evening therein, but they are brought what they desire in the world."

Al-Hasan and Qatadah and others said: "The Arabs, the most affluent among them, would have breakfast and dinner, and the Qur'an was revealed in accordance with what was in their souls of delight, so He said: ﴿And they will have their provision therein morning and evening﴾."

Abu Muhammad (Ibn Abi Hatim) said: "This is a munkar hadith."
