Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 19, verse 64–65:

Imam Ahmad said: Ya'la and Waki' narrated to us, both saying: 'Umar ibn Dharr narrated to us, from his father, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Jibril: "What prevents you from visiting us more often than you visit us?" He said: Then there was revealed ﴿And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is between that. And your Lord is not ever forgetful.﴾ to the end of the verse.

Al-Bukhari alone transmitted it. He narrated it under the tafsir of this verse from Abu Nu'aym, from 'Umar ibn Dharr, with the same chain. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir also narrated it from the hadith of 'Umar ibn Dharr. In both of them there is an addition at the end of the hadith: "So that was the answer to Muhammad (ﷺ)."

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: Jibril delayed from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) felt something of that and was grieved. Jibril came to him and said: "O Muhammad, ﴿And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is between that, and your Lord was not forgetful.﴾"

Mujahid said: Jibril stayed away from Muhammad (ﷺ) for twelve nights, and [the people] were saying [...]. When he came to him, he said: "O Jibril, you have stayed away from me until the polytheists thought every thought." Then there was revealed: ﴿And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord, to Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is between that [...] and your Lord was not forgetful.﴾ He said: And this verse is like the one in Surah ad-Duha.

Likewise Ad-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, Qatadah, As-Suddi and others said: It was revealed concerning the delay of Jibril.

Al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated from Ikrimah, who said: Jibril was slow in descending to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for forty days. Then he descended, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "You did not descend until I longed for you." Jibril said to him: "Rather, I was more longing for you, but I am commanded. So it was revealed to Jibril: Say to him: ﴿And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord⦆ the verse." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, may Allah have mercy on him, and it is gharib (strange).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Mujahid, who said: The messengers were slow to the Prophet (ﷺ), then Jibril came to him and said: "What held you back, O Jibril?" Jibril said to him: "And how would we come to you when you do not cut your nails, nor clean your knuckles, nor trim your moustaches, nor use the siwak?" Then he recited: ﴿And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord⦆ to the end of the verse.

Al-Tabarani said: Abu 'Amir al-Nahwi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Suri narrated to us, Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Rahman [al-Dimashqi] narrated to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, Tha'labah ibn Muslim informed me, from Abu Ka'b, the client of Ibn 'Abbas, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ): that Jibril was slow to him, and this was mentioned to him, and he said: "And how [could he come], when you do not clean your teeth, nor trim your nails, nor trim your moustaches, nor clean your joints?"

Likewise Imam Ahmad narrated it, from Abu al-Yaman, from Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash, with similar wording. [In its chain is Abu Ka'b, the client of Ibn 'Abbas; Abu Zur'ah said: "He is not named and is not known except in this hadith."]

Imam Ahmad said: Sayyar narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated to us, al-Mughirah ibn Habib, the son-in-law of Malik ibn Dinar, narrated to us: a shaykh from the people of Madinah narrated to me, from Umm Salamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "Prepare the gathering place for us, for an angel is going to descend to the earth, which has never descended to it before."

* *

As for His saying ﴿To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us﴾: it has been said that what is before us refers to the affairs of this world, what is behind us to the affairs of the Hereafter, and ﴿what is between that﴾ to what lies between the two blasts (of the Trumpet). This is the view of Abu al-'Aliyah, 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Qatadah in one report from them, as-Suddi, and ar-Rabi' ibn Anas.

It has also been said: ﴿what is before us﴾ is what we are going to face of the affairs of the Hereafter, ﴿what is behind us﴾ is what has passed of this world, and ﴿what is between that﴾ is what lies between this world and the Hereafter. Something similar is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj, and ath-Thawri. Ibn Jarir also chose this view, and Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And your Lord was not forgetful﴾: Mujahid [and as-Suddi] said its meaning is: your Lord did not forget you.

It has already been reported from him that this verse is like His saying: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still, your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested [you]﴾ [ad-Duha: 1-3].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yazid ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Samad al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Uthman [Ibn 'Abbas in one copy] — meaning Abu al-Jumahir — narrated to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, 'Asim ibn Raja' ibn Haywah narrated to us, from his father, from Abu al-Darda', raising it (to the Prophet ﷺ), who said: "What Allah has made lawful in His Book is lawful, what He has made unlawful is unlawful, and what He has been silent about is pardoned. So accept from Allah His pardon, for Allah would not forget anything." Then he recited this verse: ﴿And your Lord was not forgetful﴾.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them﴾ [i.e., their Creator and Regulator, the Judge over them and the One who disposes of them, whose decree none can repel], ﴿so worship Him and be steadfast in His worship. Do you know of any namesake for Him?﴾: Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "Do you know of any equal or like for the Lord?"

Likewise said Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj, and others.

'Ikrimah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "No one is named ar-Rahman except Him, Blessed and Exalted is He, and holy is His name."

As for His saying: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely gather them and the devils﴾, the Lord, blessed and exalted, swore by His noble Self that He will surely gather them all together with their devils, those whom they used to worship besides Allah. ﴿Then We will surely bring them forth around Hell, on their knees﴾.

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: it means seated, like His saying: ﴿And you will see every nation kneeling﴾ [al-Jathiyah 45:28].

As-Suddi said regarding His saying: ﴿Then We will surely bring them forth around Hell, on their knees﴾: it means standing. And it is narrated from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, the same.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then We will surely pull out from every group﴾, it means from every nation, as Mujahid said, ﴿those of them who were most insolent toward the Most Merciful﴾.

ath-Thawri said, from 'Ali ibn al-Aqmar, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The first is held back for the last, until the number is complete, and then He brings them all together. Then He begins with the greatest of them in crime, then the next greatest, and that is His saying: ﴿Then We will surely pull out from every group those of them who were most insolent toward the Most Merciful﴾.

Qatadah said regarding: ﴿Then We will surely pull out from every group those of them who were most insolent toward the Most Merciful﴾: "Then We will surely pull out from the people of every religion their leaders and chiefs in evil." Ibn Jurayj and other early scholars said the same. This is like His saying: ﴿Until, when they have all overtaken one another therein, the last of them will say of the first of them, "Our Lord, these are the ones who led us astray, so give them a double punishment of the Fire." He will say, "For each is double, but you do not know." And the first will say to the last, "You had no superiority over us, so taste the punishment for what you used to earn."﴾ [al-A'raf 7:38-39].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then indeed We are most knowing of those most deserving of burning therein﴾, the "then" (thumma) here is used to connect one report to another. The meaning is that He, the Exalted, knows best who among the servants deserves to burn in the Fire of Hell and remain in it forever, and who deserves a multiplied punishment, as He said in the previous verse: ﴿He will say, "For each is double, but you do not know."﴾

Ibn Kathir said: Allah, the Exalted, tells us that man is astonished and considers it unlikely that he will be brought back after his death, as He says: ﴿But if you are astonished, then astonishing is their saying: "When we are dust, will we indeed be in a new creation?"﴾ [al-Ra'd 13:5], and He says: ﴿Does man not see that We created him from a drop of semen, and then he is an open adversary? And he presents for Us an example and forgets his own creation. He says, "Who will give life to bones while they are decayed?" Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is Knowing of all creation."﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:77-79]. And here He says: ﴿And man says, "When I have died, will I really be brought out alive?" Does man not remember that We created him before, while he was nothing?﴾

Allah, the Exalted, uses the first creation as proof of the return. That is, He created man when he was nothing, so will He not bring him back now that he has become something? As He says: ﴿And it is He who begins the creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾ [al-Rum 30:27].

In the Sahih (of al-Bukhari) it is narrated: "Allah, the Exalted, says: The son of Adam has denied Me, though it was not for him to deny Me, and the son of Adam has harmed Me, though it was not for him to harm Me. As for his denying Me, it is his saying, 'He will not bring me back as He originated me,' and the first creation is not easier for Me than its repetition. As for his harming Me, it is his saying, 'Allah has taken a son,' while I am the One, the Eternal Refuge, who neither begets nor is begotten, and to whom no one is equal." (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4975)

* *

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 19, verse 71–72 (part 1 of 2):

Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, Khalid ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Kathir ibn Ziyad al-Barsani, from Abu Sumayyah, who said: "We disagreed about the wurud (coming to the Fire). Some of us said: No believer will enter it. Others said: They will all enter it, then Allah will save those who had taqwa (were God-fearing). So I met Jabir ibn Abdullah and said to him: 'We disagreed about the wurud.' He said: 'They will all come to it'—and Sulayman said once: 'They will all enter it'—and he pointed with his two fingers to his ears and said: 'May they be deaf, if I have not heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "No one, righteous or wicked, will remain but that he will enter it. It will be coolness and safety for the believer, just as it was for Ibrahim, to the extent that the Fire will cry out from their coolness. Then Allah will save those who had taqwa and leave the wrongdoers in it on their knees."'" (Al-Musnad, 3/328; al-Mundhiri said in al-Targhib, 2/306: "its narrators are trustworthy"). It is gharib (unusual), and they did not record it.

Al-Hasan ibn Arafah said: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Bakkar ibn Abi Marwan, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, who said: The people of Paradise, after they had entered Paradise, said: "Did not our Lord promise us the coming upon the Fire?" It was said: "You have passed by it, and it was extinguished."

Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ibn Uyaynah, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, who said: Abdullah ibn Rawahah was resting his head in his wife's lap, and he wept, and his wife wept. He said: "What makes you weep?" She said: "I saw you weeping, so I wept." He said: "I remembered the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And there is none of you but will come to it﴾, and I do not know whether I will be saved from it or not." (Tafsir Abd al-Razzaq, 2/11.) In another narration: he was ill.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Malik ibn Mighwal, from Abu Ishaq: Abu Maysarah, whenever he went to his bed, would say: "Would that my mother had not borne me," and then he would weep. It was said: "What makes you weep, O Abu Maysarah?" He said: "We were told that we will come to it, and we were not told that we will depart from it." (Tafsir al-Tabari, 16/82.)

Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said, from al-Hasan al-Basri: A man said to his brother: "Has it reached you that you will come to the Fire?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Has it reached you that you will depart from it?" He said: "No." He said: "Then why laugh?" [So he was not seen laughing until he met Allah.] (The bracketed addition is from F, A, and al-Tabari.)

Abd al-Razzaq also said: Ibn Uyaynah informed us, from Amr, who said: One who heard Ibn Abbas disputing with Nafi' ibn al-Azraq told me: Ibn Abbas said: "Does al-wurud mean entering?" Nafi' said: "No." Ibn Abbas recited: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be coming to it﴾ [al-Anbiya: 98]. "Did they come to it or not?" And he said: ﴿He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them into the Fire﴾ [Hud: 98]. "Did he lead them into it or not? As for you and me, we will enter it, so see whether we will come out of it or not. I do not think Allah will bring you out of it because of your denial." So Nafi' laughed.

Ibn Jurayj narrated, from Ata', who said: Abu Rashid al-Harouri—he is Nafi' ibn al-Azraq—said: ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾ [al-Anbiya: 102]. Ibn Abbas said: "Woe to you! Are you mad? Where is His saying: ﴿He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them into the Fire﴾ [Hud: 98], ﴿And We will drive the criminals to Hell as a herd﴾ [Maryam: 86], ﴿And there is none of you but will come to it﴾? By Allah, the supplication of those who passed was: 'O Allah, bring me out of the Fire safe, and admit me to Paradise victorious.'" (Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir, 16/82.)

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Muharibi narrated to me, Asbat narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik, from Ubayd Allah, from Mujahid, who said: I was with Ibn Abbas when a man called Abu Rashid—he is Nafi' ibn al-Azraq—came to him and said: "O Ibn Abbas, what do you say about the saying of Allah: ﴿And there is none of you but will come to it; it is a decree from your Lord, inevitably decreed﴾?" He said: "As for you and me, Abu Rashid, we will come to it. So see: will we depart from it or not?" (Tafsir al-Tabari, 16/84.)

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Shu'bah said: Abdullah ibn al-Sa'ib informed me, from one who heard Ibn Abbas recite it [thus]—(added from T, F, A)—"And there is none of them but will come to it," meaning: the disbelievers. (Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir, 16/83.)

Similarly, Amr ibn al-Walid al-Shanni (in A: "al-Sanni") narrated that he heard Ikrimah recite it thus: "And there is none of them but will come to it," and he said: "They are the wrongdoers. Thus we used to recite it." Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir.

Al-Awfi said, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And there is none of you but will come to it; it is a decree from your Lord, inevitably decreed﴾: it means the righteous and the wicked. Do you not hear the saying of Allah to Pharaoh: ﴿He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them into the Fire—and wretched is the watering place to which they are led﴾ and ﴿And We will drive the criminals to Hell as a herd﴾? He called the coming to the Fire "entering," and not "departing."

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Israil, from al-Suddi, from Murrah, from Abdullah—that is, Ibn Mas'ud—concerning ﴿And there is none of you but will come to it﴾: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The people will all come to the Fire [al-Nar] (added from T, F, A, and al-Musnad), then they will depart from it according to their deeds."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Abd ibn Humayd, from Ubayd Allah, from Israil, from al-Suddi, with the same chain. (Al-Musnad, 1/434; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3159, who said: "A hasan hadith; Shu'bah narrated it from al-Suddi without raising it [to the Prophet ﷺ].") He also narrated it by way of Shu'bah, from al-Suddi, from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, as a mawquf (ending with the companion) report. (Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3160.) [In T and F: "marfu'" (raised).]

Thus this hadith occurs here as marfu'. Asbat narrated it from al-Suddi, from Murrah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "The people will all come to the Sirat, and their coming is their standing around the Fire. Then they will depart from the Sirat according to their deeds. Some of them will pass like lightning, some like the wind, some like a bird, some like the best of horses, some like the best of camels, and some like a man running, until the last of them to pass will be a man whose light is at the places of his two big toes; he will pass, stumbling, with the Sirat being slippery and slidden, having thorns like the thorns of the saadan plant, its two sides guarded by angels who have hooks of fire with which they snatch the people." He mentioned the rest of the hadith. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Ibn Jarir said: Khallad ibn Aslam narrated to us, al-Nadr narrated to us, Israil narrated to us, Abu Ishaq informed us, from Abu al-Ahwas [the mawla of al-Ahwas in T], from Abdullah, concerning His saying: ﴿And there is none of you but will come to it﴾, he said: "The Sirat over Hell is like the edge of a sword. The first group passes like lightning, the second like the wind, the third like the best of horses, and the fourth like the best of beasts. Then they pass, while the angels say: 'O Allah, grant safety, grant safety.'"

There are witnesses to this in the two Sahihs and elsewhere, from the narrations of Anas, Abu Sa'id, Abu Hurayrah, Jabir, and other Companions, may Allah be pleased with them all. [Hadith of Anas: al-Bayhaqi narrated it in Shu'ab al-Iman, no. 367, and weakened its chain. Hadith of Abu Hurayrah: Sahih al-Bukhari no. 6573 and Sahih Muslim no. 182. Hadith of Abu Sa'id: Sahih al-Bukhari no. 6574 and Sahih Muslim no. 183.]

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub narrated to me, Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from al-Juraymi, from [Abu al-Salil] (in H: "Ibn Abi Layla"; the text here follows T, F, A, and al-Tabari), from Ghunaym ibn Qays, who said: They mentioned the coming to the Fire, and Ka'b said: "The Fire will be held back for the people as if it were the back of a melted fat, until the feet of all creation settle upon it, the righteous and the wicked. Then a caller will call to it: 'Hold back your companions and leave my companions.' Then it will swallow up every one of its allies, and it knows them better than a man knows his son. The believers will come out with their garments dripping." Ka'b said: "Between the shoulders of the keeper of its guardians there is a distance of a year's journey, and with each of them is a two-pronged club, with which he pushes and throws into the Fire seven hundred thousand." (Tafsir al-Tabari, 16/82.)

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Sufyan [in T: "Shaqiq"], from Jabir, from Umm Mubashshir, from Hafsah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I truly hope that no one who witnessed Badr and al-Hudaybiyyah will enter the Fire, God willing." She said: I said: "Does not Allah say: ﴿And there is none of you but will come to it﴾?" She said: He said: "I heard Him say: ﴿Then We will save those who had taqwa, and We will leave the wrongdoers in it on their knees.﴾" (Al-Musnad, 6/285.)

Imam Ahmad also said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Sufyan [in T: "Shaqiq"], from Jabir, from Umm Mubashshir—the wife of Zayd ibn Harithah—who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in the house of Hafsah, and he said: "No one who witnessed Badr and al-Hudaybiyyah will enter the Fire." Hafsah said: "Does not Allah say: ﴿And there is none of you but will come to it﴾?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ﴿Then We will save those who had taqwa﴾. (Al-Musnad, 6/362.)

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from Sa'id, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No Muslim will lose three children who are touched by the Fire, except as a tahillat al-qasam (a passing touch to fulfil the oath)." (Sahih al-Bukhari no. 6656; Sahih Muslim no. 2632.)

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar said: al-Zuhri informed me, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever has three [children who die] will not be touched by the Fire except as a tahillat al-qasam," meaning the wurud. (Tafsir Abd al-Razzaq, 2/11.)

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Zam'ah narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "No Muslim will lose three children who are touched by the Fire, except as a tahillat al-qasam." Al-Zuhri said: "It seems he meant this verse: ﴿And there is none of you but will come to it; it is a decree from your Lord, inevitably decreed﴾." (Musnad al-Tayalisi no. 2304.)

Ibn Jarir said: Imran ibn Bakkar al-Kala'i (in T: "al-Khala'i") narrated to me, Abu al-Mughirah (in T: "Abu Shu'bah") narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Tamim narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to visit a man from among his companions who had a fever, and I was with him. Then he said: "Allah, Exalted is He, says: 'It is My Fire, which I impose upon My believing servant, so that it may be his share of the Fire in the Hereafter.'" Gharib, and they did not record it through this route. (Tafsir al-Tabari, 6/831; al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra, 3/382, through Muhammad ibn Yahya from Abu al-Mughirah.)

And Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Uthman ibn al-Aswad, from Mujahid, who said: "Fever is every believer's share of the Fire," then he recited: "And there is none of you but will come to it."

Ibn Kathir's Commentary (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on Surah 19, verses 71–72 (part 2 of 2):

Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Zabban ibn Fa'id narrated to us, from Sahl ibn Mu'adh ibn Anas al-Juhani, from his father, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who said: "Whoever recites: ﴿Say, He is Allah, the One﴾ until he completes it ten times, Allah will build for him a palace in Paradise." Umar said: "In that case we will increase (our recitation), O Messenger of Allah!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah is more abundant and better [in giving]."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) also said: "Whoever recites a thousand verses in the way of Allah, he will be recorded on the Day of Resurrection with the Prophets, the truthful ones (al-siddiqin), the martyrs and the righteous, and excellent are those as companions, if Allah wills. And whoever stands guard behind the Muslims in the way of Allah, voluntarily and not for the wage of a ruler, he will not see the Fire with his own eyes except as the fulfilment of the oath (tahillat al-qasam). Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾. And indeed, remembrance of Allah in the way of Allah is multiplied seven hundredfold over spending." In another narration: "seven hundred thousandfold."

Abu Dawud narrated, from Abu al-Tahir, from Ibn Wahb, from Yahya ibn Ayyub and Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub, both from Zabban (in A: "Rayyan"), from Sahl, from his father, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Indeed, prayer, fasting and remembrance are multiplied seven hundredfold over spending in the way of Allah."

Abd al-Razzaq narrated, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾, he said: it is the passing over it.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said, regarding His words: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾: the coming (wurud) of the Muslims is their passing over the bridge (al-jisr) within it, and the coming of the polytheists is that they enter it. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "On that Day many will slip and stumble, and on that day two rows of angels will surround the bridge, their supplication being: O Allah, grant safety, grant safety."

As-Suddi narrated, from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding His words: ﴿It is a decree decreed by your Lord﴾, he said: an obligatory oath. Mujahid said: [hatman] means a decision (qada'). Ibn Juraij said likewise.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Then We shall save those who were righteous﴾, meaning: when all creatures have passed over the Fire, and those among the disbelievers and the sinners who are ruined by their sins have fallen into it according to their state, Allah the Exalted saves the believing, God-fearing servants from it according to their deeds. Their crossing over the Sirat and their speed is according to the deeds they did in the world. Then the sinners among the believers will be interceded for: the angels, the Prophets and the believers will intercede, and they will bring out a great multitude who have been consumed by the Fire, except the marks of their faces, which are the places of prostration. Their being brought out from the Fire is in accordance with the faith in their hearts: first they bring out whoever has in his heart the weight of a dinar of faith, then the one after him, then the one after him, until they bring out whoever has in his heart the least, least, least weight of an atom's weight of faith. Then Allah brings out from the Fire whoever has said at some time: "There is no god but Allah," even if he has done no good deed at all. None will remain in the Fire except those for whom eternal abiding is decreed, as authentic hadiths have related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This is why He the Exalted said: ﴿Then We shall save those who were righteous and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees﴾

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 19, verse 71–72 (part 1 of 2):

Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, Khalid ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Kathir ibn Ziyad al-Barsani, from Abu Sumayyah, who said: "We disagreed about the wurud (coming to the Fire). Some of us said: No believer will enter it. Others said: They will all enter it, then Allah will save those who had taqwa (were God-fearing). So I met Jabir ibn Abdullah and said to him: 'We disagreed about the wurud.' He said: 'They will all come to it'—and Sulayman said once: 'They will all enter it'—and he pointed with his two fingers to his ears and said: 'May they be deaf, if I have not heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "No one, righteous or wicked, will remain but that he will enter it. It will be coolness and safety for the believer, just as it was for Ibrahim, to the extent that the Fire will cry out from their coolness. Then Allah will save those who had taqwa and leave the wrongdoers in it on their knees."'" (Al-Musnad, 3/328; al-Mundhiri said in al-Targhib, 2/306: "its narrators are trustworthy"). It is gharib (unusual), and they did not record it.

Al-Hasan ibn Arafah said: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Bakkar ibn Abi Marwan, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, who said: The people of Paradise, after they had entered Paradise, said: "Did not our Lord promise us the coming upon the Fire?" It was said: "You have passed by it, and it was extinguished."

Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ibn Uyaynah, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, who said: Abdullah ibn Rawahah was resting his head in his wife's lap, and he wept, and his wife wept. He said: "What makes you weep?" She said: "I saw you weeping, so I wept." He said: "I remembered the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And there is none of you but will come to it﴾, and I do not know whether I will be saved from it or not." (Tafsir Abd al-Razzaq, 2/11.) In another narration: he was ill.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Malik ibn Mighwal, from Abu Ishaq: Abu Maysarah, whenever he went to his bed, would say: "Would that my mother had not borne me," and then he would weep. It was said: "What makes you weep, O Abu Maysarah?" He said: "We were told that we will come to it, and we were not told that we will depart from it." (Tafsir al-Tabari, 16/82.)

Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said, from al-Hasan al-Basri: A man said to his brother: "Has it reached you that you will come to the Fire?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Has it reached you that you will depart from it?" He said: "No." He said: "Then why laugh?" [So he was not seen laughing until he met Allah.] (The bracketed addition is from F, A, and al-Tabari.)

Abd al-Razzaq also said: Ibn Uyaynah informed us, from Amr, who said: One who heard Ibn Abbas disputing with Nafi' ibn al-Azraq told me: Ibn Abbas said: "Does al-wurud mean entering?" Nafi' said: "No." Ibn Abbas recited: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be coming to it﴾ [al-Anbiya: 98]. "Did they come to it or not?" And he said: ﴿He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them into the Fire﴾ [Hud: 98]. "Did he lead them into it or not? As for you and me, we will enter it, so see whether we will come out of it or not. I do not think Allah will bring you out of it because of your denial." So Nafi' laughed.

Ibn Jurayj narrated, from Ata', who said: Abu Rashid al-Harouri—he is Nafi' ibn al-Azraq—said: ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾ [al-Anbiya: 102]. Ibn Abbas said: "Woe to you! Are you mad? Where is His saying: ﴿He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them into the Fire﴾ [Hud: 98], ﴿And We will drive the criminals to Hell as a herd﴾ [Maryam: 86], ﴿And there is none of you but will come to it﴾? By Allah, the supplication of those who passed was: 'O Allah, bring me out of the Fire safe, and admit me to Paradise victorious.'" (Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir, 16/82.)

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Muharibi narrated to me, Asbat narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik, from Ubayd Allah, from Mujahid, who said: I was with Ibn Abbas when a man called Abu Rashid—he is Nafi' ibn al-Azraq—came to him and said: "O Ibn Abbas, what do you say about the saying of Allah: ﴿And there is none of you but will come to it; it is a decree from your Lord, inevitably decreed﴾?" He said: "As for you and me, Abu Rashid, we will come to it. So see: will we depart from it or not?" (Tafsir al-Tabari, 16/84.)

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Shu'bah said: Abdullah ibn al-Sa'ib informed me, from one who heard Ibn Abbas recite it [thus]—(added from T, F, A)—"And there is none of them but will come to it," meaning: the disbelievers. (Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir, 16/83.)

Similarly, Amr ibn al-Walid al-Shanni (in A: "al-Sanni") narrated that he heard Ikrimah recite it thus: "And there is none of them but will come to it," and he said: "They are the wrongdoers. Thus we used to recite it." Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir.

Al-Awfi said, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And there is none of you but will come to it; it is a decree from your Lord, inevitably decreed﴾: it means the righteous and the wicked. Do you not hear the saying of Allah to Pharaoh: ﴿He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them into the Fire—and wretched is the watering place to which they are led﴾ and ﴿And We will drive the criminals to Hell as a herd﴾? He called the coming to the Fire "entering," and not "departing."

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Israil, from al-Suddi, from Murrah, from Abdullah—that is, Ibn Mas'ud—concerning ﴿And there is none of you but will come to it﴾: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The people will all come to the Fire [al-Nar] (added from T, F, A, and al-Musnad), then they will depart from it according to their deeds."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Abd ibn Humayd, from Ubayd Allah, from Israil, from al-Suddi, with the same chain. (Al-Musnad, 1/434; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3159, who said: "A hasan hadith; Shu'bah narrated it from al-Suddi without raising it [to the Prophet ﷺ].") He also narrated it by way of Shu'bah, from al-Suddi, from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, as a mawquf (ending with the companion) report. (Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3160.) [In T and F: "marfu'" (raised).]

Thus this hadith occurs here as marfu'. Asbat narrated it from al-Suddi, from Murrah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "The people will all come to the Sirat, and their coming is their standing around the Fire. Then they will depart from the Sirat according to their deeds. Some of them will pass like lightning, some like the wind, some like a bird, some like the best of horses, some like the best of camels, and some like a man running, until the last of them to pass will be a man whose light is at the places of his two big toes; he will pass, stumbling, with the Sirat being slippery and slidden, having thorns like the thorns of the saadan plant, its two sides guarded by angels who have hooks of fire with which they snatch the people." He mentioned the rest of the hadith. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Ibn Jarir said: Khallad ibn Aslam narrated to us, al-Nadr narrated to us, Israil narrated to us, Abu Ishaq informed us, from Abu al-Ahwas [the mawla of al-Ahwas in T], from Abdullah, concerning His saying: ﴿And there is none of you but will come to it﴾, he said: "The Sirat over Hell is like the edge of a sword. The first group passes like lightning, the second like the wind, the third like the best of horses, and the fourth like the best of beasts. Then they pass, while the angels say: 'O Allah, grant safety, grant safety.'"

There are witnesses to this in the two Sahihs and elsewhere, from the narrations of Anas, Abu Sa'id, Abu Hurayrah, Jabir, and other Companions, may Allah be pleased with them all. [Hadith of Anas: al-Bayhaqi narrated it in Shu'ab al-Iman, no. 367, and weakened its chain. Hadith of Abu Hurayrah: Sahih al-Bukhari no. 6573 and Sahih Muslim no. 182. Hadith of Abu Sa'id: Sahih al-Bukhari no. 6574 and Sahih Muslim no. 183.]

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub narrated to me, Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from al-Juraymi, from [Abu al-Salil] (in H: "Ibn Abi Layla"; the text here follows T, F, A, and al-Tabari), from Ghunaym ibn Qays, who said: They mentioned the coming to the Fire, and Ka'b said: "The Fire will be held back for the people as if it were the back of a melted fat, until the feet of all creation settle upon it, the righteous and the wicked. Then a caller will call to it: 'Hold back your companions and leave my companions.' Then it will swallow up every one of its allies, and it knows them better than a man knows his son. The believers will come out with their garments dripping." Ka'b said: "Between the shoulders of the keeper of its guardians there is a distance of a year's journey, and with each of them is a two-pronged club, with which he pushes and throws into the Fire seven hundred thousand." (Tafsir al-Tabari, 16/82.)

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Sufyan [in T: "Shaqiq"], from Jabir, from Umm Mubashshir, from Hafsah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I truly hope that no one who witnessed Badr and al-Hudaybiyyah will enter the Fire, God willing." She said: I said: "Does not Allah say: ﴿And there is none of you but will come to it﴾?" She said: He said: "I heard Him say: ﴿Then We will save those who had taqwa, and We will leave the wrongdoers in it on their knees.﴾" (Al-Musnad, 6/285.)

Imam Ahmad also said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Sufyan [in T: "Shaqiq"], from Jabir, from Umm Mubashshir—the wife of Zayd ibn Harithah—who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in the house of Hafsah, and he said: "No one who witnessed Badr and al-Hudaybiyyah will enter the Fire." Hafsah said: "Does not Allah say: ﴿And there is none of you but will come to it﴾?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ﴿Then We will save those who had taqwa﴾. (Al-Musnad, 6/362.)

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from Sa'id, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No Muslim will lose three children who are touched by the Fire, except as a tahillat al-qasam (a passing touch to fulfil the oath)." (Sahih al-Bukhari no. 6656; Sahih Muslim no. 2632.)

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar said: al-Zuhri informed me, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever has three [children who die] will not be touched by the Fire except as a tahillat al-qasam," meaning the wurud. (Tafsir Abd al-Razzaq, 2/11.)

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Zam'ah narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "No Muslim will lose three children who are touched by the Fire, except as a tahillat al-qasam." Al-Zuhri said: "It seems he meant this verse: ﴿And there is none of you but will come to it; it is a decree from your Lord, inevitably decreed﴾." (Musnad al-Tayalisi no. 2304.)

Ibn Jarir said: Imran ibn Bakkar al-Kala'i (in T: "al-Khala'i") narrated to me, Abu al-Mughirah (in T: "Abu Shu'bah") narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Tamim narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to visit a man from among his companions who had a fever, and I was with him. Then he said: "Allah, Exalted is He, says: 'It is My Fire, which I impose upon My believing servant, so that it may be his share of the Fire in the Hereafter.'" Gharib, and they did not record it through this route. (Tafsir al-Tabari, 6/831; al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra, 3/382, through Muhammad ibn Yahya from Abu al-Mughirah.)

And Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Uthman ibn al-Aswad, from Mujahid, who said: "Fever is every believer's share of the Fire," then he recited: "And there is none of you but will come to it."

Ibn Kathir's Commentary (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on Surah 19, verses 71–72 (part 2 of 2):

Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Zabban ibn Fa'id narrated to us, from Sahl ibn Mu'adh ibn Anas al-Juhani, from his father, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who said: "Whoever recites: ﴿Say, He is Allah, the One﴾ until he completes it ten times, Allah will build for him a palace in Paradise." Umar said: "In that case we will increase (our recitation), O Messenger of Allah!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah is more abundant and better [in giving]."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) also said: "Whoever recites a thousand verses in the way of Allah, he will be recorded on the Day of Resurrection with the Prophets, the truthful ones (al-siddiqin), the martyrs and the righteous, and excellent are those as companions, if Allah wills. And whoever stands guard behind the Muslims in the way of Allah, voluntarily and not for the wage of a ruler, he will not see the Fire with his own eyes except as the fulfilment of the oath (tahillat al-qasam). Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾. And indeed, remembrance of Allah in the way of Allah is multiplied seven hundredfold over spending." In another narration: "seven hundred thousandfold."

Abu Dawud narrated, from Abu al-Tahir, from Ibn Wahb, from Yahya ibn Ayyub and Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub, both from Zabban (in A: "Rayyan"), from Sahl, from his father, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Indeed, prayer, fasting and remembrance are multiplied seven hundredfold over spending in the way of Allah."

Abd al-Razzaq narrated, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾, he said: it is the passing over it.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said, regarding His words: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾: the coming (wurud) of the Muslims is their passing over the bridge (al-jisr) within it, and the coming of the polytheists is that they enter it. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "On that Day many will slip and stumble, and on that day two rows of angels will surround the bridge, their supplication being: O Allah, grant safety, grant safety."

As-Suddi narrated, from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding His words: ﴿It is a decree decreed by your Lord﴾, he said: an obligatory oath. Mujahid said: [hatman] means a decision (qada'). Ibn Juraij said likewise.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Then We shall save those who were righteous﴾, meaning: when all creatures have passed over the Fire, and those among the disbelievers and the sinners who are ruined by their sins have fallen into it according to their state, Allah the Exalted saves the believing, God-fearing servants from it according to their deeds. Their crossing over the Sirat and their speed is according to the deeds they did in the world. Then the sinners among the believers will be interceded for: the angels, the Prophets and the believers will intercede, and they will bring out a great multitude who have been consumed by the Fire, except the marks of their faces, which are the places of prostration. Their being brought out from the Fire is in accordance with the faith in their hearts: first they bring out whoever has in his heart the weight of a dinar of faith, then the one after him, then the one after him, until they bring out whoever has in his heart the least, least, least weight of an atom's weight of faith. Then Allah brings out from the Fire whoever has said at some time: "There is no god but Allah," even if he has done no good deed at all. None will remain in the Fire except those for whom eternal abiding is decreed, as authentic hadiths have related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This is why He the Exalted said: ﴿Then We shall save those who were righteous and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees﴾

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 19, verses 73–74:

Allah, exalted is He, informs about the disbelievers: when the signs of Allah are recited to them, clear in their indication, evident in their proof, and manifest in their demonstration, they turn away from them and avert themselves. They say of those who believe, boasting over them and arguing for the soundness of their false religion, that they are: ﴿better in position and finer in assembly﴾ [meaning: better dwellings, higher abodes, and finer assembly (nadi)], and the nadi is the gathering place of men for conversation; that is, their assembly is more populous, and more frequented and visited. They mean: how could we be upon falsehood while we are in this station, whereas those (who believe) are hidden and concealed in the house of al-Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam and similar houses, upon the truth? As Allah, exalted is He, says reporting about them: ﴿And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it"﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 11]. And the people of Noah said: ﴿Shall we believe you, when the lowest have followed you?﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 111]. And He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And thus We tested some of them by means of others, that they might say, "Is it these whom Allah has favored among us?" Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ [al-An'am: 53]. Therefore Allah, exalted is He, said, refuting their doubt: ﴿And how many generations We destroyed before them⁠—﴾, meaning: how many nations and generations of deniers We have destroyed for their disbelief, ﴿who were better in furnishings and appearance﴾, meaning: they were better than these in wealth, goods, sights, and forms.

Al-A'mash related from Abu Dhabyan, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿better in position and finer in assembly﴾: he said, "al-maqam is the dwelling, and al-nadi is the gathering, al-athath is the goods, and al-ri'y is the appearance."

Al-Awfi related from Ibn Abbas: al-maqam is the dwelling, and al-nadi is the gathering, and the blessing and splendor in which they were. This is as Allah said to the people of Pharaoh when He destroyed them and related their account in the Qur'an: ﴿How many gardens and springs did they leave behind, and crops and a noble station﴾ [al-Dukhan: 25–26]. So al-maqam is the dwelling and the bounty, and al-nadi is the gathering and the assembly in which they used to meet. Allah also said, relating to His Messenger the matter of the people of Lot: ﴿and you commit the evil in your assembly﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 29]. The Arabs call the gathering an-nadi.

Qatadah said: When they saw the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ) in their living, with roughness and austerity among them, the polytheists taunted them with what you hear: ﴿Which of the two groups is better in position and finer in assembly?﴾. Likewise said Mujahid and al-Dahhak.

Among them, some said regarding al-athath that it is wealth; others said it is goods; and others said it is clothing. And al-ri'y is the appearance, as Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and others said.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: it means the forms (suwar). Likewise Malik said: ﴿athathan wa ri'yan﴾: more wealth and finer forms. All of these are close in meaning and sound.

They say of those who believe, boasting over them and arguing for the soundness of their false religion, that they are: ﴿better in position and finer in assembly﴾ [meaning: better dwellings, higher abodes, and finer assembly (nadi)], and the nadi is the gathering place of men for conversation; that is, their assembly is more populous, and more frequented and visited. This is as Allah said to the people of Pharaoh when He destroyed them and related their account in the Qur'an: ﴿How many gardens and springs did they leave behind, and crops and a noble station﴾ [al-Dukhan: 25–26]. So al-maqam is the dwelling and the bounty, and al-nadi is the gathering and the assembly in which they used to meet. Allah also said, relating to His Messenger the matter of the people of Lot: ﴿and you commit the evil in your assembly﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 29]. The Arabs call the gathering an-nadi.

Qatadah said: When they saw the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ) in their living, with roughness and austerity among them, the polytheists taunted them with what you hear: ﴿Which of the two groups is better in position and finer in assembly?﴾. Likewise said Mujahid and al-Dahhak.

Among them, some said regarding al-athath that it is wealth; others said it is goods; and others said it is clothing. And al-ri'y is the appearance, as Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and others said.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: it means the forms (suwar). Likewise Malik said: ﴿athathan wa ri'yan﴾: more wealth and finer forms. All of these are close in meaning and sound.

Ibn Kathir said: Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Say﴾ O Muhammad, to these polytheists who deny their Lord and claim that they are upon the truth while you are upon falsehood: ﴿Whoever is in error﴾, that is, from us and from you, ﴿let the Most Merciful extend for him an extension﴾, that is, the Most Merciful will grant him respite in what he is in, until he meets his Lord and his term comes to an end, ﴿either the punishment﴾ which will befall him, ﴿or the Hour﴾ which will come upon him suddenly. ﴿Then they will know﴾ at that time ﴿who is worse in position and weaker in forces﴾ [that is]: in contrast to what they argued regarding the superiority of their station and the goodliness of their assemblies.

Mujahid said concerning His words, ﴿let the Most Merciful extend for him an extension﴾: "Then Allah will leave him in his transgression." Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir (al-Tabari), may Allah have mercy on him, affirmed this interpretation.

This is a mubahala (mutual invocation of divine curse) addressed to the polytheists who claim that they are upon guidance in what they are engaged in, just as the Exalted mentioned the mubahala of the Jews in His words: ﴿Say: O you who are Jews, if you claim that you are allies of Allah to the exclusion of other people, then wish for death, if you are truthful﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 6], meaning: invoke death upon whichever of us or you is the one in falsehood, if you claim that you are upon the truth, for the invocation will not harm you. But they shrank from that. The explanation of this has already been presented at length in Surat al-Baqarah, and to Allah belongs all praise.

And just as the Exalted mentioned the mubahala with the Christians in Surat Al 'Imran, when they insisted upon disbelief, persisted in transgression and excess in their claim that Isa is the son of Allah. Allah had mentioned His proofs and evidences for the servitude of Isa, and that he is a created being like Adam. After that He said: ﴿Whoever disputes with you concerning him after knowledge has come to you, say: Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves; then let us invoke earnestly and lay the curse of Allah upon the liars﴾ [Al 'Imran: 61]. They also shrank from that.

When Allah, the Exalted, mentioned how He extends the term for those who are in misguidance in what they are engaged in, and increases them in what they are upon, He then informed of the increase in guidance for those who are guided, as He said, the Exalted: ﴿And when a surah is revealed, some of them say, "Which of you has had its faith increased by this?" As for those who believed, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice. But as for those in whose hearts is a disease, it has added defilement to their defilement, and they die while they are disbelievers﴾ [At-Tawbah: 124-125].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And the enduring good deeds﴾, its explanation and the discussion about it have already been presented, along with the hadiths related to it, in Surah al-Kahf.

﴿Better in reward with your Lord﴾, meaning, better in recompense, ﴿and better in return﴾, meaning, better in outcome and in the return they bring to their doer.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: 'Umar ibn Rashid informed us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat one day, took a dry twig and stripped its leaves, then said: "Indeed, saying: La ilaha illa Allah, Allahu akbar, al-hamdu lillah, and subhan Allah, removes sins just as the wind removes the leaves of this tree. Take them, O Abu al-Darda', before you are prevented from them. They are the enduring good deeds, and they are among the treasures of Paradise." Abu Salamah said: Whenever Abu al-Darda' mentioned this hadith, he would say: "I will surely declare the oneness of Allah (tahlil), I will surely glorify Allah (takbir), and I will surely exalt Allah (tasbih)," until when an ignorant person saw me, he thought I was insane.

This, on its apparent reading, is a mursal (a report in which a Successor narrates directly from the Prophet (ﷺ) without mentioning the Companion), but it may be from the narration of Abu Salamah from Abu al-Darda', and Allah knows best. Similarly, it occurs in Sunan Ibn Majah, from the hadith of Abu Mu'awiyah, from 'Umar ibn Rashid, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, from Abu al-Darda', and he mentioned something similar.

[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3813). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/194): "This chain is weak."]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 19, verse 77–80:

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Muslim, from Masruq, from Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, who said: "I was a blacksmith (qayn), and al-'As ibn Wa'il owed me a debt. So I came to him to demand it. He said: 'No, by Allah, I will not pay you until you disbelieve in Muhammad.' [I said: 'No, by Allah, I will not disbelieve in Muhammad (ﷺ)'] until you die and are then resurrected." He said: "When I die and am resurrected, I will come to you, and I will have wealth and children there, and then I will pay you." So Allah revealed: ﴿Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our verses and said, "I will surely be given wealth and children"?﴾ up to His words: ﴿and he will come to Us alone﴾.

It was recorded by the compilers of the Sahih (al-Bukhari and Muslim) and others, through more than one route, from al-A'mash with this chain. In the wording of al-Bukhari: "I was a blacksmith in Makkah, and I made a sword for al-'As ibn Wa'il, so I came to demand my payment." He then mentioned the hadith and said: ﴿Or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?﴾ — he said: "A pledge (mawthiq)."

Abd al-Razzaq said: al-Thawri narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, who said: Khabbab ibn al-Aratt said: "I was a blacksmith in Makkah, and I used to work for al-'As ibn Wa'il. So dirhams accumulated for me upon him, and I came to demand them. He said to me: 'I will not pay you until you disbelieve in Muhammad.' I said: 'I will not disbelieve in Muhammad until you die and are resurrected.' He said: 'When I am resurrected, I will have wealth and children.'" He said: "I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah revealed: ﴿Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our verses and said, "I will surely be given wealth and children"?﴾ up to His words: ﴿and he will come to Us alone﴾."

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Some men from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to seek payment of a debt from al-'As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi. They came to him demanding it. He said: 'Do you not claim that in Paradise there is gold, silver, silk, and all kinds of fruits?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then your promised time is the Hereafter. By Allah, I will be given wealth and children, and I will be given the like of your book which you have brought.'" So Allah struck his example in the Qur'an and said: ﴿Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our verses﴾ up to His words: ﴿and he will come to Us alone﴾.

Thus said Mujahid, Qatadah, and others: it was revealed concerning al-'As ibn Wa'il.

* *

As for His words: ﴿I will surely be given wealth and children﴾, some read "walad" with a fatha on the "waw", and others read it with a damma, and both have the same meaning. Ru'bah said:

"Praise be to Allah, the Mighty, the Sole (fardan),
who has not taken from offspring any offspring (wuldan)."

Al-Harith ibn Hillizah said:

"And indeed I have seen companions who have grown rich in wealth and offspring (walada)."

And another poet said:

"Would that so-and-so had been in his mother's womb,
and would that so-and-so had been the offspring (wuld) of a donkey."

It was said: "wuld" with a damma is a plural, and "walad" with a fatha is a singular; this is the dialect of Qays. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Has he attained knowledge of the unseen?﴾ — this is a denial against this speaker. ﴿I will surely be given wealth and children﴾ means: on the Day of Resurrection; that is, has he known what he will have in the Hereafter, so that he swears an oath about it? ﴿Or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?﴾ — or does he have a covenant with Allah that He will give him that? It has already been mentioned in al-Bukhari that it means a pledge (mawthiq).

Mujahid said: "They urge them on with urging" (tushlihim ishla').

Qatadah said: "They provoke them with provocation to the disobedience of Allah."

Sufyan al-Thawri said: "They entice them with enticement and hasten them with hastening."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So do not be hasty against them; We are only counting out for them a count﴾, meaning: Do not be hasty, O Muhammad, against these people in the occurrence of punishment upon them. ﴿We are only counting out for them a count﴾, meaning: We are only delaying them until a specified, fixed term, and they will certainly return to the punishment and retribution of Allah. ﴿And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. Ikrimah said: "ad-Didd means regret."

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says: Allah, exalted is He, informs about His friends, the righteous (al-Muttaqun), who feared Him in the worldly abode, followed His Messengers, believed them in what they reported, obeyed them in what they commanded, and refrained from what they forbade: that He will gather them on the Day of Resurrection as a delegation (wafd) to Him. A wafd are those who come riding, and from this comes the word "delegations" (al-wufud). They will ride upon she-camels (najā'ib) of light, from the mounts of the Hereafter, and they will come to the best one who is come to, to the abode of His honour and His good pleasure.

As for the criminals (al-Mujrimun), who denied the Messengers and opposed them, they will be driven to the Fire with violence, "as a thirsty herd" (wirdan), meaning thirsty. This was said by 'Ata', Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and others. And here it is said: "Which of the two groups is better in station and finer in assembly?" (Maryam: 73).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Ibn Khalid narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Qays al-Mala'i, from Ibn Marzuq, regarding "On the Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation" (Maryam: 85): He said: When the believer comes out of his grave, he will be met by the most beautiful form he has ever seen and the sweetest of scents. He will say: "Who are you?" It will say: "Do you not recognise me?" He will say: "No, except that Allah has made your scent sweet and your face beautiful." It will say: "I am your righteous deed. This is how you were in the world, of good and pleasant deeds. You have long ridden me in the world, so come, ride me." And he will ride it. That is His saying: "On the Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding "On the Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation": He said: riders.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, Ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Isma'il, from a man, from Abu Hurayrah regarding "On the Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation": He said: upon camels.

Ibn Juraij said: upon noble mounts (najā'ib).

al-Thawri said: upon she-camels (al-nuq).

Qatadah said regarding "On the Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation": to Paradise.

'Abd Allah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said in the Musnad of his father: Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Musahhir informed us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, Al-Nu'man ibn Sa'd narrated to us, who said: We were sitting with 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, when he recited this verse: "On the Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation." He said: No, by Allah, they will not be gathered on their feet, and a delegation is not gathered on their feet, but upon she-camels the like of which creation has never seen, with saddles of gold on them, and they will ride upon them until they strike the gates of Paradise.

(Zawa'id al-Musnad 1/155 and Tafsir al-Tabari 16/96.)

Thus it was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir, from the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq al-Madani, with the same chain. It adds: "Upon them are saddles of gold, and their reins are of chrysolite (zabarjad)," and the rest is similar.

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated here a very strange marfu' hadith from 'Ali, saying:

My father narrated to us, Abu Ghassan Malik ibn Isma'il al-Nahdi narrated to us, Maslamah ibn Ja'far al-Bajali narrated to us, I heard Abu Mu'adh al-Basri say: 'Ali was one day with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he recited this verse: "On the Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation." He said: "I do not think the delegation is anything but the riders, O Messenger of Allah." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, when they come out of their graves they will be met, or brought, with white she-camels having wings, upon which are saddles of gold, the straps of their sandals are light, every step of which reaches as far as the eye can see. They will reach a tree from whose root two springs gush forth. They will drink from one of them, and it will wash whatever impurity is in their bellies, and they will bathe in the other, and their skins and hair will never become disheveled after that, and the radiance of bliss will flow over them. Then they will come to the gate of Paradise, where there is a ring of red ruby upon sheets of gold, and they will strike the ring against the plate, and a resonance will be heard from it, O 'Ali, and it will reach every maiden (hawra') that her husband has come, and she will send her guardian, who will open for him. When he sees him, he will fall prostrate to him" (Maslamah said: "I think he said: 'in prostration'"). He will say: "Raise your head, for I am only your guardian, appointed over your affair." He will follow him and trace his footsteps, and the maiden will be hastened by eagerness and will come out of her tents of pearl and ruby until she embraces him. Then she will say: "You are my beloved, and I am your beloved; I am the eternal one who does not die, I am the blessed one who does not suffer distress, I am the content one who is never angry, and I am the abiding one who does not depart." He will enter a dwelling whose height from its base to its roof is a hundred thousand cubits, built upon pearl-sand, in bands of yellow, red and green, no band resembling another. In the dwelling are seventy couches, upon each couch seventy cushions, upon each cushion seventy wives, upon each wife seventy garments, and the marrow of her shin is seen through the garments. He will consummate with her in the space of a night from your nights here. Rivers flow beneath them: rivers of water that has not turned foul (he said: clear, without any turbidity in it), rivers of milk whose taste has not changed, not extracted from the udders of livestock, rivers of wine, delicious to the drinkers, not pressed by men's feet, and rivers of purified honey, not produced from the bellies of bees. They will taste the fruits, and if he wishes he will eat standing, if he wishes sitting, if he wishes reclining." Then he recited: "And near them will be its shade, and its clusters will be lowered in easy access" (al-Insan: 14). He will desire food, and a white bird will come to him, or he said: a green one, and it will raise its wings, and he will eat from its sides whatever colour he wishes. Then it will fly away and depart. The angel will enter and say: "Peace be upon you: 'This is the Paradise which you have been given as an inheritance for what you used to do'" (al-Zukhruf: 72). And if a single hair of the hawra' fell to the people of the earth, the sun would be lit by it, with blackness in light."

(Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated it in Sifat al-Jannah, no. 7, from the route of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, from al-Harith, from 'Ali, that he asked the Prophet ﷺ about this verse, and he mentioned something similar.)

This is how it occurred in this narration as a marfu' report. We have also related it in the introductions from the words of 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, in similar form, and that is closer to being sound. And Allah knows best.

He said: "Say: 'O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, I covenant with You in this worldly life that if You leave me to a deed that brings me near to evil and distances me from good, and I trust in nothing but Your mercy, then make for me with You a covenant that You will fulfil for me on the Day of Resurrection, for You do not break the promise.'"

Al-Mas'udi said: Zakariyya narrated to me, from al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, who informed us from Ibn Mas'ud, and he used to add to these: "fearful, seeking refuge, seeking forgiveness, in awe and in longing towards You."

(al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 2/377 from the route of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'd, from al-Mas'udi, from 'Awn, from al-Aswad ibn Yazid, from Ibn Mas'ud, similarly, without mentioning Abu Fakhitah, and he said: "This hadith has a sound chain, but they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it.")

Then he narrated it from another route, from al-Mas'udi, similarly.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says: Allah, exalted is He, informs about His friends, the righteous (al-Muttaqun), who feared Him in the worldly abode, followed His Messengers, believed them in what they reported, obeyed them in what they commanded, and refrained from what they forbade: that He will gather them on the Day of Resurrection as a delegation (wafd) to Him. A wafd are those who come riding, and from this comes the word "delegations" (al-wufud). They will ride upon she-camels (najā'ib) of light, from the mounts of the Hereafter, and they will come to the best one who is come to, to the abode of His honour and His good pleasure.

As for the criminals (al-Mujrimun), who denied the Messengers and opposed them, they will be driven to the Fire with violence, "as a thirsty herd" (wirdan), meaning thirsty. This was said by 'Ata', Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and others. And here it is said: "Which of the two groups is better in station and finer in assembly?" (Maryam: 73).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Ibn Khalid narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Qays al-Mala'i, from Ibn Marzuq, regarding "On the Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation" (Maryam: 85): He said: When the believer comes out of his grave, he will be met by the most beautiful form he has ever seen and the sweetest of scents. He will say: "Who are you?" It will say: "Do you not recognise me?" He will say: "No, except that Allah has made your scent sweet and your face beautiful." It will say: "I am your righteous deed. This is how you were in the world, of good and pleasant deeds. You have long ridden me in the world, so come, ride me." And he will ride it. That is His saying: "On the Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding "On the Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation": He said: riders.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, Ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Isma'il, from a man, from Abu Hurayrah regarding "On the Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation": He said: upon camels.

Ibn Juraij said: upon noble mounts (najā'ib).

al-Thawri said: upon she-camels (al-nuq).

Qatadah said regarding "On the Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation": to Paradise.

'Abd Allah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said in the Musnad of his father: Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Musahhir informed us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, Al-Nu'man ibn Sa'd narrated to us, who said: We were sitting with 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, when he recited this verse: "On the Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation." He said: No, by Allah, they will not be gathered on their feet, and a delegation is not gathered on their feet, but upon she-camels the like of which creation has never seen, with saddles of gold on them, and they will ride upon them until they strike the gates of Paradise.

(Zawa'id al-Musnad 1/155 and Tafsir al-Tabari 16/96.)

Thus it was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir, from the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq al-Madani, with the same chain. It adds: "Upon them are saddles of gold, and their reins are of chrysolite (zabarjad)," and the rest is similar.

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated here a very strange marfu' hadith from 'Ali, saying:

My father narrated to us, Abu Ghassan Malik ibn Isma'il al-Nahdi narrated to us, Maslamah ibn Ja'far al-Bajali narrated to us, I heard Abu Mu'adh al-Basri say: 'Ali was one day with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he recited this verse: "On the Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation." He said: "I do not think the delegation is anything but the riders, O Messenger of Allah." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, when they come out of their graves they will be met, or brought, with white she-camels having wings, upon which are saddles of gold, the straps of their sandals are light, every step of which reaches as far as the eye can see. They will reach a tree from whose root two springs gush forth. They will drink from one of them, and it will wash whatever impurity is in their bellies, and they will bathe in the other, and their skins and hair will never become disheveled after that, and the radiance of bliss will flow over them. Then they will come to the gate of Paradise, where there is a ring of red ruby upon sheets of gold, and they will strike the ring against the plate, and a resonance will be heard from it, O 'Ali, and it will reach every maiden (hawra') that her husband has come, and she will send her guardian, who will open for him. When he sees him, he will fall prostrate to him" (Maslamah said: "I think he said: 'in prostration'"). He will say: "Raise your head, for I am only your guardian, appointed over your affair." He will follow him and trace his footsteps, and the maiden will be hastened by eagerness and will come out of her tents of pearl and ruby until she embraces him. Then she will say: "You are my beloved, and I am your beloved; I am the eternal one who does not die, I am the blessed one who does not suffer distress, I am the content one who is never angry, and I am the abiding one who does not depart." He will enter a dwelling whose height from its base to its roof is a hundred thousand cubits, built upon pearl-sand, in bands of yellow, red and green, no band resembling another. In the dwelling are seventy couches, upon each couch seventy cushions, upon each cushion seventy wives, upon each wife seventy garments, and the marrow of her shin is seen through the garments. He will consummate with her in the space of a night from your nights here. Rivers flow beneath them: rivers of water that has not turned foul (he said: clear, without any turbidity in it), rivers of milk whose taste has not changed, not extracted from the udders of livestock, rivers of wine, delicious to the drinkers, not pressed by men's feet, and rivers of purified honey, not produced from the bellies of bees. They will taste the fruits, and if he wishes he will eat standing, if he wishes sitting, if he wishes reclining." Then he recited: "And near them will be its shade, and its clusters will be lowered in easy access" (al-Insan: 14). He will desire food, and a white bird will come to him, or he said: a green one, and it will raise its wings, and he will eat from its sides whatever colour he wishes. Then it will fly away and depart. The angel will enter and say: "Peace be upon you: 'This is the Paradise which you have been given as an inheritance for what you used to do'" (al-Zukhruf: 72). And if a single hair of the hawra' fell to the people of the earth, the sun would be lit by it, with blackness in light."

(Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated it in Sifat al-Jannah, no. 7, from the route of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, from al-Harith, from 'Ali, that he asked the Prophet ﷺ about this verse, and he mentioned something similar.)

This is how it occurred in this narration as a marfu' report. We have also related it in the introductions from the words of 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, in similar form, and that is closer to being sound. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: "And We shall drive the criminals to Hell as a thirsty herd (wirdan)", that is, thirsty.

"They will not have power of intercession": that is, they will have no one to intercede for them, as believers intercede for one another. As Allah, exalted is He, said, informing about them: "So we have no intercessors, nor any close friend" (al-Shu'ara': 100-101).

As for His saying: "Except him who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful" — this is a disjunctive exception (istithna' munqati'), meaning: "But whoever has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful." This covenant is the testimony that there is no god but Allah, and upholding its right.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding "Except him who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful": He said: The covenant is the testimony that there is no god but Allah, and disavowing any power or strength other than Allah's, and not hoping in anyone but Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Uthman ibn Khalid al-Wasiti narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Wasiti narrated to us, from al-Mas'udi, from 'Awn ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu Fakhitah, from al-Aswad ibn Yazid, who said: 'Abd Allah (meaning Ibn Mas'ud) recited this verse, "Except him who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful," then said: "Take a covenant with Allah, for Allah will say on the Day of Resurrection: 'Whoever has a covenant with Allah, let him stand up.'"
