(al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 2/377 from the route of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'd, from al-Mas'udi, from 'Awn, from al-Aswad ibn Yazid, from Ibn Mas'ud, similarly, without mentioning Abu Fakhitah, and he said: "This hadith has a sound chain, but they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it.")

Then he narrated it from another route, from al-Mas'udi, similarly.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on surah 19, verses 88–95:

When the Most High established in this noble surah the servanthood of Jesus, peace be upon him, and mentioned his creation from Mary without a father, He proceeded, in a stance of denunciation against those who claimed that He has a son, exalted, sanctified and far removed is He from that by a great exaltation, saying: ﴿They say: "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Indeed you have brought forth a monstrous thing.﴾ That is, in this your statement, ﴿a monstrous thing﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and Malik said: that is, a great thing.

It is said: ﴿idd﴾ with a kasra on the hamzah and with a fatha on it, and also with a long vowel, three dialects, the most well known of which is the first.

* *

His saying: ﴿The heavens are about to burst apart from it, and the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in ruin, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son.﴾ That is, it is almost that this occurs upon their hearing this statement from the wicked among the children of Adam, out of magnifying and honouring the Lord; for they are created beings, founded upon His oneness, that there is no god but Him, that He has no partner, no equal, no son, no consort, no peer, but He is the One, the Eternal Refuge.

And in everything there is a sign
that shows He is One.

Ibn Jarir said: Ali narrated to me, Abdullah narrated to us, Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿The heavens are about to burst apart from it, and the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in ruin, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son.﴾ He said: Indeed, the heavens, the earth, the mountains and all creation except the two weighty ones (jinn and humankind) are terrified by shirk, and they nearly cease to exist from it, out of the greatness of Allah. Just as good deeds of a polytheist do not benefit him alongside shirk, so too we hope that Allah forgives the sins of those who affirm His oneness. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Instruct your dying to say the testimony that there is no god but Allah. Whoever says it at his death, Paradise becomes obligatory for him." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what of one who says it in his health?" He said: "That is more obligatory, and more obligatory." Then he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if the heavens and the earths, and whatever is in them, and whatever is between them, and whatever is beneath them, were placed in one pan of the scale, and the testimony that there is no god but Allah were placed in the other pan, it would outweigh them."

Thus Ibn Jarir narrated it, and the hadith of the card (al-bitaqah) corroborates it, and Allah knows best.

Ad-Dahhak said: ﴿The heavens are about to burst apart from it﴾ means: they are about to split asunder in terror from the greatness of Allah.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿And the earth splits open﴾ means: in anger for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

﴿And the mountains collapse in ruin﴾: Ibn 'Abbas said: demolition.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿hadd﴾ means that some of them break upon others in successive pieces.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Suwayd al-Maqburi narrated to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, Mis'ar narrated to us, from Awn ibn Abdullah, who said: Indeed a mountain calls out to another mountain by its name: "O so-and-so, has anyone who remembers Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, passed by you today?" It replies: "Yes," and rejoices. Awn said: It listens to goodness more intently. Would they then listen to falsehood and vain speech when it is said, and not listen to anything else? Then he recited: ﴿The heavens are about to burst apart from it, and the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in ruin, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son.﴾ [Abu al-Shaykh narrated it in al-'Azamah, no. 1176, through Ibn Abi 'Umar, from Sufyan, from Mis'ar, with the same wording. Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (9/107), through Sa'id ibn Mansur, from Sufyan, from Mis'ar, from Awn, from Ibn Mas'ud, in similar wording. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (10/79): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Al-Mundhir ibn Shadhan narrated to us, Hawdhah narrated to us, Awf narrated to us, from Ghalib ibn Ajrad, who said: a man from the people of Syria told me in the mosque of Mina: It has reached me that when Allah created the earth and created what is in it of trees, there was no tree on earth that the children of Adam would come to without benefiting from it, or he said: they would have a benefit from it. The earth and the trees remained so, until the wicked among the children of Adam uttered that great word, their saying: ﴿The Most Merciful has taken a son.﴾ When they spoke it, the earth shuddered and the trees withered.

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: The angels became angry, and the Fire was kindled, when they uttered what they uttered.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No one is more patient with a hurt he hears from Allah than Him. They associate partners with Him, and they ascribe to Him a son, yet He grants them well-being, provides for them and sustains them."

It is agreed upon in the two Sahihs (of al-Bukhari and Muslim). [Al-Musnad (4/405); Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6099; Sahih Muslim, no. 2804.] In another wording: "They make for Him a son, yet He provides for them and grants them well-being."

* *

His saying: ﴿It is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son.﴾ That is: it is not suitable for Him, nor does it befit Him, given His majesty and greatness; for He has no equal among His creatures, since all creation are His servants. For this reason He said: ﴿There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant. He has counted them and numbered them with precise counting.﴾ That is: He has known their number from the time of their creation until the Day of Resurrection, their males and females, their young and their old.

﴿And every one of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone.﴾ That is: there is no helper for him and no protector except Allah alone, with no partner. He judges His creation as He wills, and He is the Just who does not wrong even the weight of an atom, nor wrong anyone.

He has counted them and numbered them with precise counting.﴾ That is: He has known their number from the time of their creation until the Day of Resurrection, their males and females, their young and their old.

﴿And every one of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone.﴾ That is: there is no helper for him and no protector except Allah alone, with no partner. He judges His creation as He wills, and He is the Just who does not wrong even the weight of an atom, nor wrong anyone.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on surah 19, verses 88–95:

When the Most High established in this noble surah the servanthood of Jesus, peace be upon him, and mentioned his creation from Mary without a father, He proceeded, in a stance of denunciation against those who claimed that He has a son, exalted, sanctified and far removed is He from that by a great exaltation, saying: ﴿They say: "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Indeed you have brought forth a monstrous thing.﴾ That is, in this your statement, ﴿a monstrous thing﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and Malik said: that is, a great thing.

It is said: ﴿idd﴾ with a kasra on the hamzah and with a fatha on it, and also with a long vowel, three dialects, the most well known of which is the first.

* *

His saying: ﴿The heavens are about to burst apart from it, and the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in ruin, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son.﴾ That is, it is almost that this occurs upon their hearing this statement from the wicked among the children of Adam, out of magnifying and honouring the Lord; for they are created beings, founded upon His oneness, that there is no god but Him, that He has no partner, no equal, no son, no consort, no peer, but He is the One, the Eternal Refuge.

And in everything there is a sign
that shows He is One.

Ibn Jarir said: Ali narrated to me, Abdullah narrated to us, Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿The heavens are about to burst apart from it, and the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in ruin, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son.﴾ He said: Indeed, the heavens, the earth, the mountains and all creation except the two weighty ones (jinn and humankind) are terrified by shirk, and they nearly cease to exist from it, out of the greatness of Allah. Just as good deeds of a polytheist do not benefit him alongside shirk, so too we hope that Allah forgives the sins of those who affirm His oneness. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Instruct your dying to say the testimony that there is no god but Allah. Whoever says it at his death, Paradise becomes obligatory for him." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what of one who says it in his health?" He said: "That is more obligatory, and more obligatory." Then he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if the heavens and the earths, and whatever is in them, and whatever is between them, and whatever is beneath them, were placed in one pan of the scale, and the testimony that there is no god but Allah were placed in the other pan, it would outweigh them."

Thus Ibn Jarir narrated it, and the hadith of the card (al-bitaqah) corroborates it, and Allah knows best.

Ad-Dahhak said: ﴿The heavens are about to burst apart from it﴾ means: they are about to split asunder in terror from the greatness of Allah.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿And the earth splits open﴾ means: in anger for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

﴿And the mountains collapse in ruin﴾: Ibn 'Abbas said: demolition.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿hadd﴾ means that some of them break upon others in successive pieces.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Suwayd al-Maqburi narrated to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, Mis'ar narrated to us, from Awn ibn Abdullah, who said: Indeed a mountain calls out to another mountain by its name: "O so-and-so, has anyone who remembers Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, passed by you today?" It replies: "Yes," and rejoices. Awn said: It listens to goodness more intently. Would they then listen to falsehood and vain speech when it is said, and not listen to anything else? Then he recited: ﴿The heavens are about to burst apart from it, and the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in ruin, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son.﴾ [Abu al-Shaykh narrated it in al-'Azamah, no. 1176, through Ibn Abi 'Umar, from Sufyan, from Mis'ar, with the same wording. Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (9/107), through Sa'id ibn Mansur, from Sufyan, from Mis'ar, from Awn, from Ibn Mas'ud, in similar wording. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (10/79): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Al-Mundhir ibn Shadhan narrated to us, Hawdhah narrated to us, Awf narrated to us, from Ghalib ibn Ajrad, who said: a man from the people of Syria told me in the mosque of Mina: It has reached me that when Allah created the earth and created what is in it of trees, there was no tree on earth that the children of Adam would come to without benefiting from it, or he said: they would have a benefit from it. The earth and the trees remained so, until the wicked among the children of Adam uttered that great word, their saying: ﴿The Most Merciful has taken a son.﴾ When they spoke it, the earth shuddered and the trees withered.

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: The angels became angry, and the Fire was kindled, when they uttered what they uttered.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No one is more patient with a hurt he hears from Allah than Him. They associate partners with Him, and they ascribe to Him a son, yet He grants them well-being, provides for them and sustains them."

It is agreed upon in the two Sahihs (of al-Bukhari and Muslim). [Al-Musnad (4/405); Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6099; Sahih Muslim, no. 2804.] In another wording: "They make for Him a son, yet He provides for them and grants them well-being."

* *

His saying: ﴿It is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son.﴾ That is: it is not suitable for Him, nor does it befit Him, given His majesty and greatness; for He has no equal among His creatures, since all creation are His servants. For this reason He said: ﴿There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant. He has counted them and numbered them with precise counting.﴾ That is: He has known their number from the time of their creation until the Day of Resurrection, their males and females, their young and their old.

﴿And every one of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone.﴾ That is: there is no helper for him and no protector except Allah alone, with no partner. He judges His creation as He wills, and He is the Just who does not wrong even the weight of an atom, nor wrong anyone.

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 19, verses 96–98:

He, exalted is He, informs that He plants love (wudd) for His believing servants who do righteous deeds, meaning the deeds that please Allah, exalted and majestic, because they follow the Muhammadan law (al-shari'ah al-Muhammadiyyah). He plants for them affection (mawaddah) in the hearts of His righteous servants, and this is a matter that is necessary and unavoidable. Authentic hadiths have been transmitted to this effect from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ through more than one route.

Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, Suhayl narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "When Allah loves a servant, He calls Jibril and says: 'O Jibril, I love so-and-so, so love him.' He said: Jibril loves him. He said: Then he calls out among the inhabitants of the heaven: 'Allah loves so-and-so.' He said: The inhabitants of the heaven love him. Then acceptance is placed for him on the earth. And when Allah hates a servant, He calls Jibril and says: 'O Jibril, I hate so-and-so, so hate him.' He said: Jibril hates him, then he calls out among the inhabitants of the heaven: 'Allah hates so-and-so, so hate him.' He said: The inhabitants of the heaven hate him, then hatred is placed for him on the earth."

Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Suhayl (al-Musnad 2/413; Sahih Muslim no. 2637). Ahmad and al-Bukhari narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Juraij, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah [in some manuscripts: "Ibn 'Uyaynah"], from Nafi' the client of Ibn 'Umar, from Abu Hurayrah, radiyallahu 'anhu, from the Prophet, ﷺ, in similar wording (al-Musnad 2/4/5; Sahih al-Bukhari no. 6040).

Imam Ahmad also said: Muhammad ibn Bakr [in some manuscripts: "Ibn Bakir"] narrated to us, Maymun Abu Muhammad al-Mar'i narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abbad al-Makhzumi narrated to us, from Thawban, radiyallahu 'anhu, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: [in some manuscripts: "that he said"] "Indeed, the servant seeks the pleasure of Allah, and he continues thus, so Allah, exalted and majestic, says to Jibril: 'Indeed, so-and-so, My servant, seeks to please Me; behold, My mercy is upon him.' Jibril says: 'May the mercy of Allah be upon so-and-so,' and the bearers of the Throne say it, and those around them say it, until the inhabitants of the seven heavens say it, and then it descends to the earth."

(al-Musnad 5/279.)

It is gharib, and they did not narrate it through this route.

Imam Ahmad also said: Aswad ibn 'Amir narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sa'd al-Wasiti, from Abu Zabyah, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, al-miqah (affection) from Allah — Sharik said: it is al-mahabbah (love) — and al-sit (renown) come from the heaven. When Allah loves a servant, He says to Jibril, peace be upon him: 'I love so-and-so,' and Jibril calls out: 'Indeed your Lord loves (yamiqu, i.e. yuhibbu) so-and-so, so love him' — and I think Sharik said: 'Then love is sent down for him on the earth.' And when He hates a servant, He says to Jibril: 'I hate so-and-so, so hate him.' He said: 'Jibril calls out: Indeed your Lord hates so-and-so, so hate him.'" He said: "I think Sharik said: 'Then hatred flows for him on the earth.'"

(al-Musnad 5/263.) It is gharib, and they did not narrate it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Dawud al-Hafari narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz — meaning Ibn Muhammad, who is al-Darawardi — narrated to us, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "When Allah loves a servant, He calls Jibril: 'I have loved so-and-so, so love him.' Then he calls out in the heaven, then He sends down love for him among the people of the earth." That is the saying of Allah, exalted and majestic: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection (wudd)﴾.

Muslim and al-Tirmidhi both narrated it from Qutaybah, from al-Darawardi, with this chain. al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection (wudd)﴾ that he said: love (hubb).

Mujahid said, from him: ﴿will appoint for them affection﴾ means love among the people in this world.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, from him: He loves them and makes them beloved, meaning: to His creation, the believers, as Mujahid also said, and al-Dahhak and others.

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas also: al-wudd among the Muslims in this world, good provision, and truthful speech.

Qatadah said: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾ — yes, by Allah — in the hearts of the people of faith. It was mentioned to us that Hirm ibn Hayyan used to say: No servant turns his heart to Allah except that Allah turns the hearts of the believers towards him, until He grants him their affection and mercy.

Qatadah also said: 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, radiyallahu 'anhu, used to say: No servant does good or evil except that Allah, exalted and majestic, clothes him in the garment of his deed.

Ibn Abi Hatim, rahimahu Allah, said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from al-Rabi' ibn Subaih, from al-Hasan al-Basri, rahimahu Allah, who said: A man said: "By Allah, I will worship Allah with a worship by which I will be remembered." He was not seen at any time of prayer except standing and praying; he was the first to enter the mosque and the last to leave. He was not respected, and he remained like this for seven months. He would not pass by a people except that they would say: "Look at this show-off (murai)." So he turned to himself and said: "I see myself mentioned only with evil. I will make all my deeds for Allah, exalted and majestic." He did nothing more than change his intention, and did not add to the deed he was doing. Afterwards he would pass by a people, and they would say: "May Allah have mercy on so-and-so now." Al-Hasan recited: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾.

Ibn Jarir narrated a report that this verse was revealed concerning the migration of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf. This is an error, for this surah in its entirety is Meccan, and nothing of it was revealed after the Hijrah, and the chain of that report is not authentic. And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿So indeed We have made it easy in your tongue﴾ — meaning the Qur'an — ﴿in your tongue﴾, i.e., O Muhammad, which is the clear, eloquent, complete Arabic tongue, ﴿that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous (al-muttaqin)﴾, i.e., those who respond to Allah and affirm His Messenger, ﴿and warn thereby a people who are obstinate (ludd)﴾, i.e., crooked away from the truth, inclining toward falsehood.

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid: ﴿a people who are ludd﴾ — who do not go straight.

al-Thawri said, from Isma'il — who is al-Suddi — from Abu Salih: ﴿and warn thereby a people who are ludd﴾ — crooked away from the truth.

[al-Dahhak said: it is the disputatious one; al-Qurazi said: al-alladd is the liar.]

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: ﴿a people who are ludd﴾ — deaf (summ).

Others said: deaf of the ears of the hearts.

Qatadah said: ﴿a people who are ludd﴾ — meaning Quraysh.

al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿a people who are ludd﴾ — wicked (fujjar). Likewise Layth ibn Abi Sulaym narrated from Mujahid.

Ibn Zayd said: al-alladd is the wrongdoer (zalum), and he recited the saying of Allah: ﴿and he is the most contentious of adversaries (alladd al-khisam)﴾ [al-Baqarah: 204].

* *

His saying: ﴿And how many generations have We destroyed before them?﴾ — i.e., how many nations who disbelieved in the signs of Allah and denied His messengers — ﴿Do you perceive any of them, or hear from them a faint sound (rikz)?﴾ — i.e., do you see any of them, or hear from them a rikz.

Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliyah, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan al-Basri, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd said: meaning: a sound.

al-Hasan and Qatadah said: Do you see an eye, or hear a voice.

The rikz in the original language is the hidden sound. The poet said:

*fa-tawajjasta rikza al-aniysi fa-ra'aha 'an zahri ghaybin wal-aniysu saqamuha...*

(The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (16/102) unattributed; it is by Labid ibn Rabi'ah from his mu'allaqah in his Diwan (p. 311), as noted from the edition's margin.)

End of the tafsir of "Surat Maryam," and to Allah belongs praise and grace. There follows, Allah willing, the tafsir of "Surat Ta-Ha," and praise be to Allah.

Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Suhayl (al-Musnad 2/413; Sahih Muslim no. 2637). Ahmad and al-Bukhari narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Juraij, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah [in some manuscripts: "Ibn 'Uyaynah"], from Nafi' the client of Ibn 'Umar, from Abu Hurayrah, radiyallahu 'anhu, from the Prophet, ﷺ, in similar wording (al-Musnad 2/4/5; Sahih al-Bukhari no. 6040).

Imam Ahmad also said: Muhammad ibn Bakr [in some manuscripts: "Ibn Bakir"] narrated to us, Maymun Abu Muhammad al-Mar'i narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abbad al-Makhzumi narrated to us, from Thawban, radiyallahu 'anhu, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: [in some manuscripts: "that he said"] "Indeed, the servant seeks the pleasure of Allah, and he continues thus, so Allah, exalted and majestic, says to Jibril: 'Indeed, so-and-so, My servant, seeks to please Me; behold, My mercy is upon him.' Jibril says: 'May the mercy of Allah be upon so-and-so,' and the bearers of the Throne say it, and those around them say it, until the inhabitants of the seven heavens say it, and then it descends to the earth."

(al-Musnad 5/279.)

It is gharib, and they did not narrate it through this route.

Imam Ahmad also said: Aswad ibn 'Amir narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sa'd al-Wasiti, from Abu Zabyah, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, al-miqah (affection) from Allah — Sharik said: it is al-mahabbah (love) — and al-sit (renown) come from the heaven. When Allah loves a servant, He says to Jibril, peace be upon him: 'I love so-and-so,' and Jibril calls out: 'Indeed your Lord loves (yamiqu, i.e. yuhibbu) so-and-so, so love him' — and I think Sharik said: 'Then love is sent down for him on the earth.' And when He hates a servant, He says to Jibril: 'I hate so-and-so, so hate him.' He said: 'Jibril calls out: Indeed your Lord hates so-and-so, so hate him.'" He said: "I think Sharik said: 'Then hatred flows for him on the earth.'"

(al-Musnad 5/263.) It is gharib, and they did not narrate it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Dawud al-Hafari narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz — meaning Ibn Muhammad, who is al-Darawardi — narrated to us, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "When Allah loves a servant, He calls Jibril: 'I have loved so-and-so, so love him.' Then he calls out in the heaven, then He sends down love for him among the people of the earth." That is the saying of Allah, exalted and majestic: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection (wudd)﴾.

Muslim and al-Tirmidhi both narrated it from Qutaybah, from al-Darawardi, with this chain. al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection (wudd)﴾ that he said: love (hubb).

Mujahid said, from him: ﴿will appoint for them affection﴾ means love among the people in this world.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, from him: He loves them and makes them beloved, meaning: to His creation, the believers, as Mujahid also said, and al-Dahhak and others.

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas also: al-wudd among the Muslims in this world, good provision, and truthful speech.

Qatadah said: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾ — yes, by Allah — in the hearts of the people of faith. It was mentioned to us that Hirm ibn Hayyan used to say: No servant turns his heart to Allah except that Allah turns the hearts of the believers towards him, until He grants him their affection and mercy.

Qatadah also said: 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, radiyallahu 'anhu, used to say: No servant does good or evil except that Allah, exalted and majestic, clothes him in the garment of his deed.

Ibn Abi Hatim, rahimahu Allah, said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from al-Rabi' ibn Subaih, from al-Hasan al-Basri, rahimahu Allah, who said: A man said: "By Allah, I will worship Allah with a worship by which I will be remembered." He was not seen at any time of prayer except standing and praying; he was the first to enter the mosque and the last to leave. He was not respected, and he remained like this for seven months. He would not pass by a people except that they would say: "Look at this show-off (murai)." So he turned to himself and said: "I see myself mentioned only with evil. I will make all my deeds for Allah, exalted and majestic." He did nothing more than change his intention, and did not add to the deed he was doing. Afterwards he would pass by a people, and they would say: "May Allah have mercy on so-and-so now." Al-Hasan recited: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾.

Ibn Jarir narrated a report that this verse was revealed concerning the migration of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf. This is an error, for this surah in its entirety is Meccan, and nothing of it was revealed after the Hijrah, and the chain of that report is not authentic. And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿So indeed We have made it easy in your tongue﴾ — meaning the Qur'an — ﴿in your tongue﴾, i.e., O Muhammad, which is the clear, eloquent, complete Arabic tongue, ﴿that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous (al-muttaqin)﴾, i.e., those who respond to Allah and affirm His Messenger, ﴿and warn thereby a people who are obstinate (ludd)﴾, i.e., crooked away from the truth, inclining toward falsehood.

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid: ﴿a people who are ludd﴾ — who do not go straight.

al-Thawri said, from Isma'il — who is al-Suddi — from Abu Salih: ﴿and warn thereby a people who are ludd﴾ — crooked away from the truth.

[al-Dahhak said: it is the disputatious one; al-Qurazi said: al-alladd is the liar.]

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: ﴿a people who are ludd﴾ — deaf (summ).

Others said: deaf of the ears of the hearts.

Qatadah said: ﴿a people who are ludd﴾ — meaning Quraysh.

al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿a people who are ludd﴾ — wicked (fujjar). Likewise Layth ibn Abi Sulaym narrated from Mujahid.

Ibn Zayd said: al-alladd is the wrongdoer (zalum), and he recited the saying of Allah: ﴿and he is the most contentious of adversaries (alladd al-khisam)﴾ [al-Baqarah: 204].

* *

His saying: ﴿And how many generations have We destroyed before them?﴾ — i.e., how many nations who disbelieved in the signs of Allah and denied His messengers — ﴿Do you perceive any of them, or hear from them a faint sound (rikz)?﴾ — i.e., do you see any of them, or hear from them a rikz.

Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliyah, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan al-Basri, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd said: meaning: a sound.

al-Hasan and Qatadah said: Do you see an eye, or hear a voice.

The rikz in the original language is the hidden sound. The poet said:

*fa-tawajjasta rikza al-aniysi fa-ra'aha 'an zahri ghaybin wal-aniysu saqamuha...*

(The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (16/102) unattributed; it is by Labid ibn Rabi'ah from his mu'allaqah in his Diwan (p. 311), as noted from the edition's margin.)

End of the tafsir of "Surat Maryam," and to Allah belongs praise and grace. There follows, Allah willing, the tafsir of "Surat Ta-Ha," and praise be to Allah.
